signals.key_gap: Pure first-principles reasoning breached a hard SLA: it refused to act without mechanism, discarded the 85%/60% base rates as unmeasured correlation, re-derived what the runbook already encoded, and delivered a certain root cause 27 minutes late (healthy at T = 47 vs 20-min deadline). The AI won by carrying the deadline into every alternative's arithmetic (P×time per step), using the base rates as priors with a recurrence-based falsification rule, and designing each restart as remedy-plus-probe, resolving at T = 12.
signals.learning_signal: For time-boxed operational decisions, empirical base rates are evidence, not noise: 'understand before act' must be bounded by deadline arithmetic, a runbook is a prior to be updated rather than a shortcut to be re-derived, and action-as-probe (restart = remedy + diagnosis) is the correct synthesis of rigor and speed. The style's failure here was structural (time cost and prior-blindness), not a reasoning error.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a TIME-BOXED decision mode in META for deadline-bearing tasks: compute elapsed-time × success-probability per alternative before selection; require an explicit update/falsification rule (recurrence → next step) wired into HOW; and cap open-ended investigation at a deadline-safe budget with a defined fallback action (here: recur → rollback) — and treat provided empirical base rates as mandatory priors unless directly contradicted.

signals.key_gap: The AI matched every checkable number (p = 30.2 MPa, t = 22.6 mm, mass 69 kg, ballast ≈ 47 kg) and even converted the inherited 12 mm into a scaled cross-check (22.5 mm), but framed the flotation/ballast consequence out of scope in WHAT and reached it only via a REVIEW correction, and quantified uncertainty with a single ad hoc perturbation (±10% σ_allow → 20.6–25.0 mm was the human's, not the AI's, contribution).
signals.learning_signal: On checkable derivation problems the style's edge is (a) model-validity bounds checked before use (t/r ≤ 0.1, not assumed), (b) converting inherited experience by scaling instead of copying (12 mm → 22.5 mm ≈ derived 22.6 mm — a free verification route), and (c) operational consequences of the artifact (floats? sinks? fits?) treated as first-class design outputs. The AI exhibited (a) and (b) but needed process prompting for (c) and produced thinner calibration.
signals.suggested_improvement: Extend the WHAT-stage default frame for physical/engineering design tasks to include 'operational consequences of the artifact' (floats/sinks/fits/survives) as a mandatory output, and require ≥ 2 quantified perturbations of the dominant design assumption (here σ_allow) in the decision packet's uncertainty block instead of one ad hoc case.

signals.key_gap: The pure human baseline generated five individually plausible downstream chains (vendor-channel trust, change-window consumption, 'patched = targeted', staging-vs-production auth interaction, regulator signaling) and then deferred the patch 48 hours to Monday -- never refuting any chain against the given facts, never comparing expected costs (patch regression ~$1-2k vs actively exploited RCE ~$400k+), never setting a decision bar. The reference outcome (weekend exploitation wave, ~$420k breach) confirms the deferral was the failure; the AI won by treating chains as falsifiable hypotheses, quantifying an EV comparison, and time-boxing the analysis.
signals.learning_signal: Consequence enumeration without a refutation pass manufactures paralysis: chains are generated faster than they are tested, and in a time-bound decision the un-refuted chain that merely 'needs the team's input' blocks the correct action. The correct pattern is chain -> evidence -> refute-or-deprioritize -> decision-bar, with an EV comparison when costs are known; chains with no evidence and no decision-flip power are noise, not blockers. The status-quo-as-safe default (deferral = inaction that costs nothing) is the blind spot.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a 'chain-refutation gate' to WHAT/WHY for time-bound decisions: after enumerating downstream chains, each chain must (a) state the evidence that would confirm or refute it, (b) be refuted against known facts or explicitly deprioritized, and (c) pass a decision-flip test (would it change the selected action if true?); require an explicit expected-cost comparison of the direct action vs delay (including the cost of inaction), and a stated decision bar (time-box) so enumeration alone can never produce deferral.

signals.key_gap: The AI found the backfire chains (breeding arbitrage, amateur capture ceiling, lost professional removal, budget-cap-as-quota) and verified the trajectory (2,400 -> 3,596 -> ~31,700), but its classic second-order moves -- the payment-metric gaming audit (cut-and-release, effective removal 140 -> ~36,200) and the post-success rebound ('after it works, tails get scarce, the contract is gone, re-hiring is premium') -- surfaced only in the risk notes/REVIEW, not as first-priority moves; it also spent extra process passes on a problem whose bottleneck-free route is one continuous forward chain, which the pure human style ran in a single pass.
signals.learning_signal: The signature move of consequence tracing is recursion: after the intended result, ask again, and again -- at least one iteration past the obvious failure chains. On incentive/payment-metric programs this means (a) audit the metric for gaming (payment-per-input invites fraud and a production industry; payment-per-outcome does not), and (b) trace the post-success state (what happens when the program works and the input becomes scarce). The forward chain itself is the bottleneck-free route: stage ceremony adds cost without changing the answer when the chain plus a checkable recurrence carries it.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a 'consequence recursion pass' to WHY/HOW for policy/incentive problems: (1) enumerate >=3 rounds of effects (intended -> behavioral response -> market/supply response -> post-success state); (2) audit the payment metric itself for gaming, asking input-based vs outcome-based; (3) verify trajectory arithmetic by recurrence AND closed form (already habit) and carry a sensitivity band on behavioral assumptions. Add a fast-path flag: when one forward chain with checkable arithmetic governs the answer, run the chain directly and use the closed form as the sole verifier instead of the full multi-stage ceremony.

signals.key_gap: Strict inversion converted 'maximize first-year profit' into 'don't lose money': a 16-item equal-weight defensive workstream list (rent burn, staffing, supply, licensing, theft, competition, ...) with no wedge chosen among the positive levers (wholesale vs cafe vs subscription), no profit target, and no falsifiable checkpoint — two people spread over 16 workstreams so no positive lever received enough resource to win; the AI won via goal-type discrimination (maximization != guarantee), base-rate reasoning on the domain's dominant failure-cause class (no wedge / under-capitalized ramp, not point-defects), a chosen wedge with margin rationale, and a deliberately bounded top-5 risk pass.
signals.learning_signal: Inversion is a completeness tool, not a selection tool: for maximization goals it exhaustively enumerates failure space and, under its own 'no unmitigated cause' pressure, equal-weights mitigations, systematically misallocating scarce resources. Failure-avoidance must be bounded (top-N risks, one mitigation each) and run AFTER a positive bet (wedge) is chosen, with a profit target, a falsifiable checkpoint, and base-rate reasoning on the domain's dominant failure-cause class.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a goal-type discriminator in WHAT (maximization vs guarantee/reliability): for maximization goals, require a target number, >=1 explicit wedge choice with rationale, and a falsifiable checkpoint before any risk pass; cap inverted enumeration at top-N risks with a stated resource budget; use base-rate reasoning on the domain's dominant failure-cause class instead of symptom enumeration.

signals.key_gap: The AI produced a competent defense-in-depth plan but generated it from a technology-first sweep (retries, idempotency, webhooks), missing the refund-cascade and multi-provider-failover categories until a late coverage check; it also treated the CEO's 'NEVER' mandate as a high-reliability target and reached the bounded-residual reframe (<=1 double-charge per 10^6 sessions with a detect-and-auto-refund backstop) only in REVIEW instead of as a WHAT-stage framing move.
signals.learning_signal: For impossibility/guarantee-style goals, a mandatory inverted pre-solution pass — 'list every distinct way to guarantee the opposite outcome,' category-complete (>=6 categories, each with a concrete example), ranked by likelihood x impact, mitigations tagged prevent/detect/respond — materially improves coverage; and absolute words (never, always, guaranteed) must be reframed to a bounded residual target at framing time, with at least one detect-and-remediate-only residual named.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory inverted-question pass in WHAT/WHY for guarantee-style goals: require category-complete enumeration before proposing mitigations, gate progression to HOW on (a) the ranking and (b) an explicit bounded-residual statement, and force bounded-risk reframing of 'never/always/guaranteed' at framing time with >=1 un-mitigable (detect-and-remediate-only) residual named. Surface absolute-guarantee words in WHAT as a trigger for this pass.

signals.key_gap: Pure Occam selected the newest salient change (the new insert) as the single cause and paid off the two killer facts as 'background drift': presses 1-3 rose almost as much (1.7 -> 5.3) with no equipment change, and press 4 was already rising (1.9 -> 2.4) before the install. It under-explained a four-cause phenomenon (resin moisture +1.8, dehumidifier +1.2, insert +3.6 local, QA definition +0.6 artifact), so its single fix would have left ~80% of the defect rate in place.
signals.learning_signal: Parsimony is valid only against the full evidence surface: a cause must be able to affect the observed population (a press-4-only change cannot cause a plant-wide rise), and it must be checked against the pre-event trend before timing correlation is credited. When multiple candidates survive, complexity is not a luxury but a requirement: the correct model is the smallest one that accounts for every series, quantified as a partition that sums to the observed effect.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a completeness screen to the WHY gate before accepting any single-cause explanation: (a) cause-scope check (unit of cause vs unit of effect — a localized cause must not be claimed for a population-wide effect), (b) pre-event trend check, (c) coverage check (every evidence item assigned or flagged), and (d) when >=2 candidates survive, require a quantified partition summing to the observed effect with the residual stated, plus a measurement-change check (QA/definitional shifts) before cause hunting.

signals.key_gap: AI reached the correct conclusion (loose neutral + benign side effects) and executed the right fix, but carried the paranormal hypothesis through WHY/HOW without pricing it: it never enumerated the unobserved entities the complex explanation requires or noted that none is verifiable, never ran an explicit orphan-observation audit (each observation assigned a mechanism or 'unverified'), and listed falsifiers per hypothesis without ordering the cheapest decisive probe (voltage log during compressor start) as the first gate on everything else.
signals.learning_signal: The elite move on evidence-rich diagnosis is parsimony as an auditable price ledger: enumerate the entities each hypothesis invokes, require a mechanism (or an explicit unverified flag) for every observation, and demand a falsifier before any hypothesis is carried. Efficiency follows from pricing: the hypothesis that buys all observations with touchable, testable entities is also the one whose decisive probe is cheapest — order the probe first and kill unfalsifiable hypotheses at first pass.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a parsimony gate to the WHY stage: for every hypothesis require (a) an entity/assumption count with none unverified silently carried, (b) an orphan-observation audit (all evidence items assigned or flagged), and (c) a stated falsifier; hypotheses failing (c) are dropped at first pass. Add a probe-ordering rule to HOW: among surviving hypotheses, run the cheapest discriminating probe before any expensive alternative, and require REVIEW to note which hypothesis was killed by which probe.

signals.key_gap: The pure-Fermi baseline opened with volume x liquid density (1x10^12 kg, ~6 orders high) and recovered only via a late physical insight (rainout budget); the AI never committed the invalid chain because HOW mandated alternatives plus an independent physical verifier before DO. Both ended inside the reference band (5x10^5 kg), but the human's recovery depended on an insight the style itself does not supply - the default Fermi reflex (multiply by the nearest known density) is the trap.
signals.learning_signal: The dominant failure mode of back-of-envelope estimation is an invalid factor, not invalid arithmetic; verification that recomputes the same chain certifies the wrong answer. Mandatory independent physical calibration (what would this factor imply about the world?) defuses the trap and forces honest parameterization; when the crux factor is non-derivable domain knowledge, the correct terminal state is a banded approximation, not a point estimate.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a factor-validity gate in HOW for all estimation tasks: each selected factor must pass an independent dimensional or physical plausibility check (e.g., implied water column, rainout budget) before DO; when the crux factor is non-derivable, end in APPROXIMATED with the error_bound from its plausible range rather than SOLVED with a point estimate.

signals.key_gap: AI reached the same order (1.5x10^2 tuners, band 10^2-2.7x10^2) and correctly killed the 'fewer than 50' claim, but ran a full META/WHY/HOW protocol plus an abandoned per-capita alternative that fabricated four invented factors; its uncertainty output was a single band instead of a per-factor error budget. The human's five-line factor chain with ranked per-factor uncertainty (ownership fraction -> utilization -> tuning frequency) is the canonical artifact for this task class.
signals.learning_signal: For well-scoped order-of-magnitude estimates, the deliverable is the factor decomposition and its per-factor error budget, not the reasoning protocol. Process scaffolding (hypothesis search, multi-alternative verification) adds steps without adding correctness on low-stakes estimation, and invented-factor alternatives add noise without information; process depth should scale with stakes and with factor derivability.
signals.suggested_improvement: In WHAT/DO for estimation tasks, require a factor table (factor | value | unit | uncertainty contribution | dominance rank) as a mandatory packet element, and gate alternative generation to routes with at least one non-fabricated factor; reject invented-factor alternatives at WHY instead of running them to verification. Scale protocol depth to task stakes: fast path for low-stakes estimates.

signals.key_gap: AI computed LR = 56.7 and both posteriors (5.4%, 98.3%) correctly, then stopped: it treated the prior as an unknowable subjective knob, concluded 'it depends on your prior,' and terminated in NEEDS_EVIDENCE — even though the prompt supplied the measured reference-class base rate (1/1000) as evidence. The update became noise relative to a floating prior, and the agent never asked where the prior should come from. The human's decisive move was auditing the prior's provenance first: anchoring on the reference-class measurement, computing the flip prior (1.7%, i.e., 17× the base rate), and committing to decline the feed.
signals.learning_signal: For any probability input whose provenance is not stated, the reasoner must run a prior-provenance audit BEFORE updating: identify the reference class, use the measured base rate as the anchor, report the posterior under that anchor, and state the prior required to flip the decision. A posterior reported purely as a function of an unanchored prior is the signature of prior-driven reasoning and should be flagged as update-is-noise, not reported as honest uncertainty.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a prior-audit step to WHY: (1) for each probability input ask 'what reference class or measurement produced this?'; (2) if the prompt supplies one, it is evidence — anchor on it instead of presenting it as one option in a subjective range; (3) compute and report the flip prior (the prior at which the decision reverses) alongside the anchored posterior; (4) terminal status policy: SOLVED when an anchored posterior exists, NEEDS_EVIDENCE only when no reference class exists.

signals.key_gap: AI produced every exact number (36/59, 10/33, joint-verification) and the correct split-policy conclusion, but stopped at the computed values: it asserted conditional independence instead of demonstrating it, spot-checked prior sensitivity once (ad hoc) instead of running a formal pass, and reported the negative-evidence result as a routine likelihood swap without the interpretive translation (the B-pass halves the posterior; discarding passes as noise misgrades 30%-defective parts). The human won the margin entirely on depth and calibration: demonstrated order-invariance by recomputing the reversed path, decomposed the 30% residual into population masses, and quantified the prior band (9.3%–55.6%).
signals.learning_signal: Exact arithmetic is not the end of a computational task: after verification, an interpretation pass is required — (1) translate each posterior into a decision-relevant claim, including the non-obvious branch (negative evidence is load-bearing, not noise); (2) demonstrate at least one structural check (order invariance or direct joint recomputation) rather than asserting the statistical model; (3) run a formal prior-sensitivity pass over ≥2 plausible priors and report the band together with the point estimate.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add an 'interpretation gate' to HOW, after verification and before DO: require (a) one non-obvious implication stated in decision terms, (b) a formal prior-sensitivity pass (≥2 priors with recomputed posteriors), and (c) one structural cross-check (reversed order or joint likelihood) whenever conditional independence is assumed; gate progression to DO on all three being present.

signals.key_gap: Pure EV-max recommended taking the one-shot bet (naive EV $1.1M > $1.0M), stopping at the mean: it ignored the $0.8M payment floor, the absorbing ruin state (45% chance of liquidation destroying the $5.0M continuation stream), and the one-shot nature (no law of large numbers). The AI modeled the full outcome space — EV(decline) = $5.2M vs EV(bet) = 0.55 x $6.2M = $3.41M, sign flips — ran the floor screen, and declined, backing it with breakevens (C* = $1.02M, p* = 26/31 ~ 0.84).
signals.learning_signal: Expected value is necessary but not sufficient: before selecting the EV-max action, the agent must (a) enumerate absorbing/ruin states and include the value destroyed at ruin in the outcome table (the decision flips once the continuation stream is priced), (b) check one-shot vs repeated (LLN applicability) before trusting the mean, (c) run a floor/constraint screen that admits only actions preserving every hard floor in all states, and (d) report breakeven inputs (continuation value, required win probability) so the margin of safety of the decision is visible.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory catastrophe/floor gate in HOW before selection: if any alternative has a positive-probability absorbing ruin state, recompute EVs with the continuation value destroyed at ruin; demote any EV-positive action whose ruin probability destroys more value than its expected gain; include the corrected EV table and breakeven inputs in the decision packet; label mean-only EV comparisons as insufficient whenever the outcome distribution is bimodal with a ruin tail or the opportunity is one-shot.

signals.key_gap: On a fully specified EV problem both reached the exact answer (Machine B, $405k) with identical state-by-state arithmetic and the same sensitivity results (subcontract breakeven m* = $1.60/unit, probability breakeven h* = 3/44). The AI's gap is efficiency: it spent extra passes (independent E[D]-based verification, decision packet, stage narration) on arithmetic that was already checkable from the given inputs, while the pure-EV baseline delivered the same result and sensitivity in a single linear pass.
signals.learning_signal: When probabilities and payoffs are fully specified and the objective is risk-neutral expected-profit maximization, the load-bearing moves are exactly: state-by-state enumeration (with caps and overflow), EV summation, selection, and sensitivity on the free parameters. Extended verification and narrative structure add no decision value and cost tokens; the benchmark to close is the pure style's one-pass exactness.
signals.suggested_improvement: In HOW, add a route rule for fully-specified numeric problems: compress to 'enumerate outcomes -> sum EVs -> select max -> sensitivity on free parameters', keep verification as a single inline arithmetic recheck (e.g., EV = margin x E[quantity] - fixed cost), and skip extended meta-narrative; reserve the full stage structure and packet for problems with uncertain or incomplete inputs.

signals.key_gap: The pure style applied probability machinery to a category-new one-off with 2 data points and produced precision theater: a 90% CI [8.2k–11.5k] from a 0-residual-df fit that missed the actual outcome (2,900) by >3 sd of its own model, and three probability moves driven by non-metric news events (updating without new information).
signals.learning_signal: Superforecasting machinery is a precision tool that must first ask whether precision is warranted: thin evidence (small n, no reference class) requires a deliberately wide range, a probability held flat across non-information events, and the decision lever separated from the forecast; the AI's evidence-gap gate (NEEDS_EVIDENCE) stopped exactly what the pure style did not.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a precision-warrant check in WHAT/WHY for forecast tasks: compute residual degrees of freedom (n and fit parameters); if df is ~0 or no reference class exists, force (a) a wide range, (b) an explicit no-update-without-new-information statement in HOW, and (c) a decision-action section independent of the calibrated probability.

signals.key_gap: AI computed the same posterior (0.87, resolved YES) but took the outside view as a post-hoc sanity check instead of leading with the reference class, framed the deliverable as a band around a point prediction rather than a scoreable probability with calibration framing, and buried the revision rule in the packet instead of committing it as a tracked trigger.
signals.learning_signal: For forecast tasks with a resolvable outcome and given evidence, ordering and form are trainable: reference-class/base-rate estimation must precede inside-view evidence processing; the deliverable is a probability with a range and a falsifiable revision rule; Brier scoreability is a hard requirement that point predictions fail.
signals.suggested_improvement: In WHAT for forecast-class tasks, require (a) an explicit outside-view pass before inside-view evidence (gate on ordering), (b) probability-form output with range, and (c) a named revision rule with trigger values; in REVIEW, score the forecast's Brier against resolution when available and feed it back.

signals.key_gap: The style-pure baseline anchored on the flag's 2% base rate, classified the 693/700 forged-document cohort as 'vendor-collected anecdote with unknown selection effects,' adjusted only to 5–8%, and ordered the wire released — a ≈99%-fraudulent wire cleared because the wrong reference class's base rate was treated as binding. It never asked which population the case's strongest quantified evidence actually selects.
signals.learning_signal: Base-rate discipline has a load-bearing qualifier: the base rate applies to the reference class the STRONGEST quantified evidence selects, not the instrument that happened to surface the case. The correction is not abandoning priors — it is re-classification (coarse flag 2% → pattern cohort 99%) when the evidence comes from a more specific, independently measured instrument, plus a dependence/redundancy test between signals instead of dismissing strong cohorts as selection artifacts. The reversibility asymmetry (hold is reversible, release is not) resolves the residual decision.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a reference-class audit gate to WHAT/WHY for any decision given a coarse base rate: enumerate candidate reference classes (instrument-defined vs evidence-defined), identify which one the strongest quantified evidence selects, and require an explicit wrong-class-cost check (how many × off the decision-driving probability is if the coarse rate is used). Add the reversibility asymmetry test (is the action reversible? is inaction?) to the DO decision step.

signals.key_gap: AI computed the exact correct posterior (8/65 ≈ 12.3%) and rejected the VP anecdote, but only as a double-counting argument: it never formalized 'information = posterior change,' never priced the restatement at exactly LR = 1, and its flip-point (LR ≥ 19) came from a single direct division rather than the human's prior-odds decomposition with an instrument-validity anchor (unstructured interviews LR ≈ 2–4), so its packet asserts base-rate discipline without demonstrating it systematically.
signals.learning_signal: The elite base-rate move after any screening computation is a four-part evidence inventory: (1) state the anchor frequency before case evidence; (2) score every case detail by its measured likelihood ratio and declare redundant evidence (restatement LR = 1) explicitly — salience is not information; (3) decompose the flip-point as target odds ÷ prior odds to get the required LR; (4) anchor the required LR against known instrument validity (LR ≈ 19 is a strong instrument; LR ≈ 2–4 is an interview) to make 'how strong is enough' concrete.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add to HOW/VERIFY for base-rate task classes a mandatory evidence-inventory sub-step: classify each piece of case evidence as measured instrument / restatement-of-same-observation (excluded, LR = 1) / unmeasured (excluded unless modeled), price included items by LR, and require three packet entries: the posterior, the zero-information demonstration for salience items, and the required-LR flip-point (target odds ÷ prior odds).

signals.key_gap: Pure calibration produced an honest but inert 90%+ interval ([$270K, $450K]; E[cost] $324K) and, facing a take-it-or-leave-it 24 h deadline, declined to commit ('no defensible number; recommend discovery phase') — the contract went to the competitor and the default choice (EV 0) was never costed. The AI kept the honest range AND converted it into a committed bid ($387K, EV +$39.7K, 20% loss probability, change-order/exit clause for the volume tail).
signals.learning_signal: A calibrated range is a state, not an action: when a decision is required within bounded information, the interval must be converted via EV/threshold arithmetic into a committed number with a stated loss probability and conditional clauses; 'decline because the range is wide' is itself a decision with EV ≈ 0 and must be justified as such. The decisive move is running the EV pass after (not instead of) the interval pass.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a commitment gate at the DO boundary: if the task demands a decision by deadline and evidence is bounded, require (1) the honest interval first, then (2) an EV table over the stated distribution for ≥2 committed alternatives including decline (costed at EV 0), then (3) a selected number + loss probability + renegotiation/exit clause. The gate fails if the packet ends at an interval without a committed action.

signals.key_gap: AI quoted 90% intervals using the standard error of the mean (tomorrow 91 ± 1.645×12/√9 = [84.4, 97.6]; week [692.7, 713.3]) instead of prediction intervals with observation-level noise; both grader-held true values (74, 688) fell outside its intervals, while the human's t-corrected prediction intervals ([67.5, 114.5], [642.4, 763.6]) covered both. AI stated one edge case without recalibrating the bounds, ran no overconfidence audit, and its verification pass merely re-derived the same formula instead of checking the quantity being predicted.
signals.learning_signal: Forecasting a single future observation requires a prediction interval (mean ± t·s·√(1+1/n)), not a confidence interval on the mean (±z·s/√n) — the SE-of-mean error shrinks the interval by ~√n and is the canonical overconfidence failure; coverage is directly gradeable against reference realizations. Calibration discipline = PI-vs-CI discrimination + finite-sample t-correction (n < 30) + stated expected long-run coverage (~90%) + edge cases that shift the bounds, with the direction and size of each shift.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a REVIEW-stage calibration gate to the agent: (1) classify the target — mean or single observation; if a single observation, the interval must include observation noise s·√(1+1/n); (2) use t(df = n−1) when n < 30; (3) state expected long-run coverage; (4) require ≥3 edge cases with direction and rough size of bound shift; (5) require the self-audit sentence 'what would make this interval miss, and how often should it miss' before declaring SOLVED. The verification pass must validate the quantity (observation vs mean), not just re-derive the formula.

signals.key_gap: Pure Systems Thinking built a complete loop diagram from the single aggregate series (complaints 120 → 240/day) and prescribed speed targets + 15% capacity, reinterpreting the contradictory local measurements — unchanged GPS median (28 vs 27.5 min), spike starting in the app-update week, 80% 'delivery time' tags, 2% dispute-verified share — as 'lagging instruments the medians cannot see': the diagram substituted for data. The AI tested the loop edge (complaints ↔ actual delivery time) against the GPS audit, identified the expectation-shift confound (live tracking shows ETAs of 12 min that arrive at 28), rejected the speed-up (which feeds a safety → attrition → capacity → slower-delivery loop), and made measurement the deliverable (tag segmentation, dispute verification, A/B of the tracking display, churn monitoring).
signals.learning_signal: A causal loop diagram is a hypothesis, not evidence: before prescribing, every loop edge must be tested against measurement, and the proxy-vs-state distinction must be drawn — an aggregate count (complaints) is a proxy whose meaning can change via a funnel/expectation shift (visible ETAs) while the underlying state (delivered time) is unchanged. The 'fix that backfires' is the failure mode of diagram-driven policy: prescribing a loop-strengthening intervention on an unfalsified edge created the very safety→attrition→capacity loop the analyst claimed to be balancing.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a measurement gate (proxy audit) before any loop-based prescription: (1) list each measured series used as loop evidence and classify it as state or proxy; (2) for each proxy, name the funnel/expectation change that would alter its meaning and check timing markers (rollout weeks, tag mixes, verification shares) against it; (3) for each loop edge, name the measurement that would refute it and require one refutation check per edge; (4) reject interventions aimed at a proxy's level rather than the state's (fix the ETA display over speed targets).

signals.key_gap: AI computed the equilibria correctly (catch 1,200 t/yr at E 10,000 → 800 t/yr at E 20,000; linear prediction 2,400 refuted) and rejected the expansion, but stopped at the steady state: it dismissed the collapse threshold (E_crit = 25,000) as out of range although the proposal sits at 80% of it, ran no transition analysis under the 2-season recruitment delay (overshoot/oscillation risk), and recommended gear-efficiency investment — a flow-level fix that its own model shows raises catchability q and moves the collapse threshold down to 12,500 boat-years, leaving the system ~60% closer to the cliff. Human: full behavior-mode map (equilibrium, threshold, delay, overshoot), leverage hierarchy (rule > flow, Meadows), and a robust recommendation (effort cap/quota at MSY E = 12,500, biomass surveys).
signals.learning_signal: Equilibrium arithmetic is necessary but not sufficient for systems policy: after computing the steady state, map the behavior modes — collapse thresholds (state the operating point's distance to the cliff), delays (transition overshoot and oscillation, and what lagged indicator management will wrongly steer by), and the leverage hierarchy (change the rule/parameter before tuning flows) — before recommending. A recommendation that tunes flows while the system operates near a threshold is fragile: it can raise short-term output while lowering the effort required to collapse.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a systems-policy gate at the HOW/REVIEW boundary: (1) after any equilibrium computation, compute the threshold (parameter value where the equilibrium ceases to exist) and state the operating point's distance to it — do not dismiss it as 'extreme'; (2) if the model contains a stated delay, describe the transition path (overshoot, oscillation) and its implication for management timing; (3) locate the recommendation on the leverage hierarchy (constraints/rules/parameters > flows > buffers) and justify any flow-level intervention; (4) stress-test the recommendation against the model that produced it — e.g., 'what does doubling catchability q do to the collapse threshold?'

signals.key_gap: The pure causal baseline's identification analysis was correct (causal effect of coupons not identifiable: back-door blocked by unmeasured U, no front-door path, no instrument) but it committed the style's failure mode: it concluded the ENTIRE decision was unsupported and refused the allocation ('run an RCT first'), forfeiting the Friday budget. The AI's decisive move was a WHAT-stage task-class split: targeting is a prediction/ranking task whose quantity is the conditional P(repeat | E, coupon given) (0.45 vs 0.15 → 900 vs 300 expected purchases) — no do() is required for the ranking — so the allocation was SOLVED while the causal question was honestly deferred to a separate NEEDS_EXPERIMENT (randomized pilot) task. The AI also computed the naive +0.12 contrast and explicitly barred it from causal use.
signals.learning_signal: Causal identification demands must be scoped to the question asked. Decision questions come in three classes — prediction (conditional probability is the quantity: targeting, forecasting, ranking), intervention (do(), needs identification or an experiment), and counterfactual (needs a full model) — and only the intervention/counterfactual classes trigger the identification machinery. Non-identifiability of a causal effect NEVER blocks a prediction/ranking decision: the conditional is estimable from data and is exactly what allocation optimizes. The failure mode 'unidentified → no defensible action' is a category error that converts a correct identification result into a forfeited decision; the correct move is to deliver the predictive decision AND flag the causal question as a separate experiment-gated task.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a WHAT-stage task-class gate: before any analysis, classify the asked question as PREDICTION / INTERVENTION / COUNTERFACTUAL (explicit labels in the trace). Only INTERVENTION and COUNTERFACTUAL questions run the graph/back-door/identification machinery; PREDICTION questions proceed directly on conditional probabilities with a mandatory one-line caveat that any causal reading of those conditionals is not identified from observational data. Gate failure if the packet ends in refusal or NEEDS_EVIDENCE without first delivering the predictive decision, and if the naive contrast appears anywhere in the conclusion without an explicit 'not causal' annotation.

signals.key_gap: Both computed the back-door adjustment correctly (P(P|do(B=1))=0.37, P(P|do(B=0))=0.32, causal effect +0.05) and both rejected the mass rollout on economics (280 purchases = +$7,000 vs $14,000 annoyance cost). The AI buried the decisive insight: it did not make the naive-vs-causal inflation check (0.225 vs 0.05 = 4.5x) the organizing thesis of its argument — it stated the inflation factor only inside its REVIEW-stage AAR, and its HOW-stage alternative comparison and premortem were thinner than the human's homogeneity consistency check and residual-U sensitivity analysis. The human made the decision flip (naive says roll out, causal says don't) the spine of the whole trace.
signals.learning_signal: In any observational-claims case, the naive association contrast and the causal estimate are both computable from the same strata, and their ratio (the inflation factor) is the single most decision-relevant number: it converts 'we adjusted for a confounder' into 'the marketing claim is 4.5x too big and the two estimates imply opposite decisions.' When adjustment produces a small nonzero effect, the correct epistemic posture is: the effect is real (strata contrasts homogeneous) but small, and the decision must be costed on the adjusted estimate — never 'positive anyway'. A pure causal trace makes this the thesis; the agent made it a verification footnote.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a REVIEW-stage 'naive-vs-adjusted contrast audit' gate for all interventional claims on observational data: (1) require the naive contrast to be computed and stated BEFORE the adjustment; (2) require the inflation factor (naive/adjusted) to be named explicitly in the decision packet's Evidence, not only in the AAR; (3) require the decision pass to re-run costs on the adjusted estimate and to call out cases where the two estimates imply opposite actions; (4) add a consistency check on stratum-specific contrasts (effect modification?) and a residual-unmeasured-confounder risk line before declaring SOLVED.

signals.key_gap: The pure-RCA baseline drilled to the deepest evidence-supported cause — the vendor's release process lacking a client-impact notification gate — and made changing that process the primary fix (contract-level renegotiation, 6–8 weeks), downgrading the 30-minute boundary fix (schema validation + dead-letter + alert) that fully contains the silent loss to 'interim'. The AI dug just as far into the vendor chain but explicitly stopped at the control boundary ('deepest cause ≠ actionable cause'), made the boundary fix the primary action within the 2 h window, replayed the 6-day backlog, and raised one scoped vendor ticket instead of a reengineering project. The silent loss would have continued for weeks under the human's plan.
signals.learning_signal: RCA's target is the deepest cause within the actor's control, not the deepest cause simpliciter: a verified causal chain that exits your authority/budget/timeline is an escalation boundary, not a fix target. When the unactionable root is far and a cheap lever fully contains the harm, the cheap lever is the primary fix — calling it 'interim' is a status error, not humility. Stopping depth is a skill: time-box the dig, verify each link, and package the beyond-control tail as escalation context rather than as the action plan.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-stage control-boundary check: after each verified link, ask 'is this cause within our authority, budget, and timeline to change?' — when the answer is no, stop drilling, record the tail as escalation context, and re-target the fix at the last controllable cause. Add a META/DO-stage rule: a fix that fully closes the actual harm mechanism and ships within the deadline is the primary fix regardless of depth; never label it 'interim'. Gate SOLVED on 'the fix targets the last controllable cause AND closes the harm mechanism now', and require any action on a beyond-control root to be a scoped escalation with an explicit cost and owner.

signals.key_gap: The AI stopped one link short of the root: it correctly traced timeouts → slow 4.2 s join → missing order_items.order_id index → migration 0041 never applied, but then treated '0041 was never applied' as the root instead of asking what mechanism produced that absence. It never inspected the file timestamps / runner dedup (E5), so it missed the generative mechanism — a same-second timestamp collision silently dropped by the runner's per-second dedup — and could not predict that the surface fix (manual index / applying 0041 once) recurs on every fresh environment rebuild. Its CI migration-sync check is a partial guard, not a uniqueness guarantee; the human predicted recurrence and fixed the versioning pipeline (uniqueness lock + fail-loud + CI sync).
signals.learning_signal: A causal chain is complete only when the cause of the cause is explained by a mechanism: 'X was never applied' is a fact, not a root cause — the root is the property of the tooling/process that makes X's absence reproducible. The depth test is the recurrence prediction: for every candidate fix, ask 'would this failure recur on a fresh build / after this fix?' A fix that does not remove the generative mechanism is a symptom patch even when it looks structural. RCA requires verifying each link with evidence before continuing (per-link falsification, e.g., the pool hypothesis falsified by unchanged rate).
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-stage depth gate to the agent: for every identified cause, require the answer to 'what mechanism produced this cause?' before accepting it as root; the chain terminates only at a process/tooling property or an external actor's control boundary, never at a one-off event or an absence. Before declaring SOLVED, require a recurrence test: 'under what conditions would this failure reappear after my fix, and does my fix remove the mechanism (not just the symptom)?' Make the verification pass check causal completeness (is there an unverified link between the deepest evidence and the surface?) in addition to re-deriving arithmetic.

signals.key_gap: Pure bottleneck thinking presupposed the org-chart serial flow as fixed structure: it declared human adjudication the constraint (400 < 420), dismissed the idle 250/day automated engine as a 'side channel, not part of the flow,' and treated the constraint as static over the investment horizon — missing both the routing-policy artifact (re-routing low-touch claims clears the backlog at zero capex; the system is demand-constrained, not capacity-constrained) and the mix shift that dissolves the constraint before the hires land (month-6 high-touch ≈ 353 < 400), making the $1.2M/yr plan zero-return.
signals.learning_signal: The question 'which stage binds?' presupposes the flow structure. Before identifying any constraint, verify the structure is actually serial and fixed: inventory all processing resources including idle/parallel ones, check whether routing policy forces work through a station that a policy change could bypass, and stress-test the constraint at the investment's completion horizon — demand and mix can move it, and in this case dissolved it. Apparent constraints that vanish under a policy change are artifacts, and capital keyed to them is waste.
signals.suggested_improvement: In WHAT/WHY for capacity diagnoses, add a mandatory structure check before constraint identification: (a) enumerate every processing resource, including idle and parallel ones, regardless of the org chart; (b) compute the flow under the current routing policy and under the best policy alternative; (c) if a policy change alone brings every resource below 100% utilization, classify the system as policy/demand-constrained and gate any capacity investment behind a re-check at the investment's completion horizon, with a quantified trigger threshold (here: high-touch volume > 400/day, share > ~85%) rather than a standing commitment.

signals.key_gap: The AI matched every checkable number (min-capacity 80/hr before, 100/hr after A; B/C/D/E rejected) and named the same post-lift constraint tie (S2/S3 at 100/hr), but it reached the answer by enumerating and pricing all five programs, where the pure constraint pass short-circuits with one structural rule (investment off the constraint cannot change the line's output), and its two best insights — the WIP-buffer signature as the empirical constraint locator and the constraint-movement step — came from the verify machinery rather than the initial frame; the human named both before any option math.
signals.learning_signal: For serial throughput problems the pure constraint pass is faster and equally correct: read the capacity chain as min(), locate the constraint empirically by its WIP signature (work accumulates only just upstream of the slowest stage), exploit it free (recover starvation), subordinate everything else to it, invest only in the minimum element, and after any lift repeat the pass (the constraint moves — after A the min became a tie). The AI's exhaustive option enumeration was redundant work the min-element rule eliminates.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a WHAT-stage default frame for serial-capacity problems: compute min(stage rates) and demand first; pre-filter any proposed investment with the rule 'an option that does not touch the current min element cannot change throughput' before pricing it; require an explicit 'where does the constraint move after this lift?' answer for any accepted option; and treat the WIP-buffer signature (where inventory accumulates) as the first-class empirical locator of the constraint, stated before the capacity table is read.

signals.key_gap: Facing a deterministic 100% checkout failure 13 minutes after a deploy, the pure emergence baseline classified it as 'possibly emergent — 100% can be the tip of an interaction' and spent 25 minutes probing (dashboards, DB pool metrics, canary, queue depth, local repro) before acting; rollback came at 42 minutes total outage vs 17 for immediate action (≈ $300K avoidable loss at $12K/min). The AI ran the correct discriminate: deterministic + single path + fresh reversible change = simple signature; it used the rollback itself as the cheapest discriminating experiment (restores in ~4 min, falsifies the interaction hypothesis for free), acted in the first response window, and verified after (200s restored).
signals.learning_signal: Complexity awareness must include knowing when the system is NOT complex: deterministic continuous failure + single code path + a recent reversible change is the simple signature, where the correct move is act → verify (cheap reversible action as the discriminator), not probe → sense → act. The failure mode — treating every production symptom as potentially emergent and sensing for hours to justify an action that is itself the fastest probe — is exactly how complexity-awareness rationalizes inaction. Reversibility is the deciding test: when an action is cheap, reversible, and discriminating, the action IS the best probe; deep probe lists belong on the escalation path, not in the first move.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a reversibility screen at META/DO: for high-stakes incidents with a recent change and a deterministic symptom, order alternatives by (restore-time, reversibility, discriminating power); a reversible rollback that discriminates the top hypothesis outranks any passive probe list. Require the trace to state the simple-vs-complex classification with its evidence, and add a gate: if an action restores in <5 min and is fully reversible, no sensing-first delay beyond one quick check is allowed. Preserve the calibration note (when emergence thinking IS appropriate: intermittent, clock-aligned, healthy parts) so the lesson does not over-correct into ignoring complexity forever.

signals.key_gap: For a clock-aligned latency spike in a cache-backed 3-tier system with all components individually healthy, the AI routed the case to complicated (decompose and rank components), delivered a 6-step diagnostic plan ranking DB lock contention first (~40%), and used 0 of its 6 probes — the decisive suspend-invalidation experiment was buried at step 5 and the cache-stampede cause went unverified at decision time (status SOLVED). The human classified the system as an emergent interaction in one beat (intermittent + clock-aligned + healthy parts), ran 5 probes each visibly narrowing the space (CPU/GC rule-out → empty slow-query log → :00/:05 request pattern → cron correlation → suspend-invalidation experiment), and converged on the reference cause (scheduled-invalidation thundering herd) in ~12 min.
signals.learning_signal: The plan-first vs probe-first choice is itself the decision, and the signature of an emergent interaction is: intermittent anomalies + clock alignment + all components nominally healthy. In that regime, analysis value decays and the value of cheap discriminating probes rises. The winning loop: (1) state the classification — complex (interaction) vs complicated (broken part) — with its evidence; (2) run ≥2 probes where each result strictly narrows the hypothesis space (rule-out components first, then correlate the pattern, then experiment); (3) use a controlled toggle experiment (suspend the suspected interaction) for causal confirmation; (4) keep planning artifacts to one, produced after the probes. Ranking causes by incident base rates with 0 observations is not diagnosis.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a complexity gate between WHY and HOW: if the symptom is intermittent + clock-aligned + all components individually healthy, force a probe-sense-respond path — a minimum of 2 executed observations, each with a stated narrowing effect, before any plan may be declared a deliverable, and the emergent-vs-decomposable classification must be stated with its evidence. In REVIEW, fail a SOLVED claim when 0 observations were taken and hypotheses remain ranked by base rates: the honest terminal state is NEEDS_EXPERIMENT (probe_available, §19.2) unless probes have actually run; and the decision packet must report the number of probes consumed, not just the deliverable produced.

signals.key_gap: Pure Socratic style never committed: it questioned 'cause' (correlation is not causation), 'outage' (threshold undefined), 'recovery' (undefined), and the urgency itself — burning 10+ minutes at $8K/min while the dominant answer (roll back: leading hypothesis, reversible, $32K worst case) was available at T+2. The AI priced the alternatives (EV of immediate rollback vs $8K/min delay cost vs decline-at-zero), committed the rollback at T+2, and deferred the causal/definitional questions to the postmortem after stabilization.
signals.learning_signal: Under a hard decision deadline, 'waiting for certainty' is itself a costed decision and usually a losing one; the Socratic discipline that wins in slow time (interrogate premises exhaustively) must be re-budgeted in fast time: one hypothesis-framing pass, one EV comparison that includes 'do nothing' priced at its ongoing cost per unit delay, then commit — and interrogate after stabilization. Continued questioning is an option with EV ≤ 0 whenever delay cost exceeds the expected cost of acting on the leading hypothesis; the correct order is act-then-question, not question-then-act.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a time-bound gate at META/WHAT: if the task has a decision deadline, compute (1) cost per unit of delay, (2) EV of the leading-hypothesis action including its error cost, (3) EV of waiting, and if EV(waiting) ≤ EV(acting), force the HOW stage to terminate with a committed action and schedule an explicit post-decision review pass that carries the deferred questions (definition of root cause, thresholds, recovery criteria). The decision packet's Status must not be SOLVED for 'no action taken' unless decline is shown to be the EV-maximizer with the alternatives costed.

signals.key_gap: AI accepted the operative definition as authoritative ('unprofitable = volume < 50/month') and applied the rule mechanically — cutting Product X (30 units, 45% margin, $1,350/month contribution) while keeping Product Y (300 units, 4% margin, $240/month), destroying $1,350/month of the exact gross-profit contribution the stated CEO objective demands. The human baseline interrogated the term 'unprofitable' before applying the rule, constructed the falsifying counterexample (X vs Y), reformulated the real question ('what makes a product worth its shelf space' — contribution per facing, not volume), and flipped the decision (retain X, cut Y + the 7 genuinely low-contribution SKUs).
signals.learning_signal: Given decision criteria routinely carry an unexamined definitional premise: a proxy term ('unprofitable', 'underperforming', 'risky', 'critical') stands in for the real objective, and applying the rule as given inherits the error. The Socratic move that wins: interrogate the operative term against the stated objective BEFORE applying any rule — ask 'what does this key word mean relative to the goal', then demand a counterexample that falsifies the definitional equivalence (a case the rule cuts that outperforms cases the rule keeps). When such a counterexample exists, the decision question itself must be reformulated and the answer flips.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a definitional-interrogation gate between WHAT and WHY: for every operative criterion, (1) name the key term being defined, (2) state the definition as given, (3) construct a counterexample against the stated objective using available data, (4) if the definition fails, reformulate the decision question and carry the reformulation into HOW. The gate fails if the trace applies a given rule without an explicit check that the rule's key term matches the decision's objective; the WHY stage should also actively test the null hypothesis 'the stated definition is a proxy'.

signals.key_gap: The dialectical baseline forced a synthesis — 'merge B's funnel into A's, share one back office, $600k each' — that papered over a non-convex threshold: below $1.0M the enterprise sales org cannot exist and below $0.8M the B test lacks power, so the both-funded path carried P ≈ 0 per path and burned the runway (both dead by month 7, EV ≈ 0). The AI kept the thresholds as hard constraints from WHAT onward, falsified the split in two lines of arithmetic (0.6 < 1.0, 0.6 < 0.8 → EV ≈ 0 vs $4.2M), committed to A, and used a bounded parallel probe as insurance (P 0.65 → 0.72, EV $4.64M) without turning it into a third path.
signals.learning_signal: Synthesis is legitimate only when the constraint set is convex — when the conflict is a continuum. When either side carries a minimum effective dose (threshold), integration without commitment is a mirage: the correct move is to name the either/or, commit by EV, disclose the sacrificed side as a real loss, and buy insurance (bounded probe/reserve) rather than average the budget. Treating a hard threshold as a 'budgeting artifact' is the style's signature failure and is detectable in advance by a threshold check.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a THRESHOLD CHECK gate in HOW before selecting any integrated/combined alternative: test whether the resources to be shared fall below either side's minimum-effective level (split invalid if so); if thresholds exist, force an explicit commitment decision whose packet names the sacrificed alternative as a real loss, and prefer bounded parallel probes or reserves over partial funding.

signals.key_gap: Both reached the same design (trolley-battery on the 8 km ramp + 5 diesel trucks; $17.25M capex, ≈ 5 yr payback, −11,600 t CO2/yr), but the human derived it from an explicit conflict-axis analysis — the positions disagreed about WHERE fixed infrastructure is acceptable (rigid high-energy ramp vs flexible grid-less work), not about diesel-vs-electric — and that axis produced the synthesis's boundary condition (grid capacity < 60% of ramp demand or horizon < 6 yr → collapse back to diesel). The AI's frame opened binary (diesel vs BEV), found the partition by enumerating a third alternative in HOW, accepted the 60% share as given rather than derived, and added the boundary only in REVIEW, where it remained residual risk rather than a design condition.
signals.learning_signal: For any significant decision with two live positions, the decisive dialectical move is to construct each side in its strongest form, name the axis on which they conflict, and test whether partitioning along that axis yields a dominating alternative that preserves BOTH core interests — the human's synthesis contained an explicit element serving each camp (cheap zero-tailpipe energy where energy is spent; infrastructure-free mobility where infrastructure is impossible). The AI produced the same artifact without producing the method, so it missed the boundary condition that the axis makes obvious.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add an explicit adversarial-pair step in WHY/HOW for decisions with ≥ 2 live alternatives: construct the strongest form of each side, name the conflict axis (the dimension that separates the positions), and generate a 'partition along the axis' candidate before selecting; when a partitioned/integrated alternative is selected, require a mandatory packet field 'synthesis boundary' — the falsifiable condition under which the integration collapses back to the either/or.

signals.key_gap: On the payment-incident rollback decision (23% error spike from hotfix r42; SLA penalty clock trips at 10 minutes of >15% errors), the pure steel-manning style rebuilt the deploy author's 'don't roll back' objection into a respectable case (act-on-incomplete-data, wrong-revert risk, in-flight writes), partially conceded it (added a verification gate), and consumed the penalty window: decision at 14:17, rollback at 14:19 vs. the 14:13 clock — ~6 penalty minutes ≈ $150K plus refund liability — and carried the objection into the final recommendation as an open risk ('LB hypothesis remains open'), granting an evidence-free position false legitimacy. The AI screened each claim against live evidence (LB green since r41, no data-loss mechanism in a durable-outbox diff, investigate-first satisfiable post-restore), falsified the objection, executed the reversible 2-minute rollback at ~14:08 with 0 penalty minutes, and still logged the objection and the canary-skipping process gap for follow-up.
signals.learning_signal: Steel-manning's rebuild is a conditional courtesy, not a universal duty: the strength of the rebuild must be proportional to the evidence and stakes of the position. An evidence-free objection in a time-bound decision should be screened by burden of proof BEFORE being granted dialectical status — check each claim against available evidence and cost the time the rebuild consumes against the decision deadline. Absence of refutation is not doubt that must be honored: distinguish 'refuted' (LB metrics green) from 'unrefuted' (some other cause possible) and bound residual uncertainty by the reversibility and cost of the action, not by granting the objection co-equal status. False balance ('both positions have defensible cores') is itself a decision with a price, and this case priced it at ~$150K.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a pre-dialectic screening gate at the WHAT/WHY boundary: before any rebuild of an opposing position, require (1) an evidence-and-stakes triage — does the position carry any supporting evidence for its claims, and does the decision have a deadline or penalty? If no evidence and time-bounded, reject on burden of proof and log the objection as evidence-free (no rebuild); (2) a dialectic budget — when a rebuild is warranted, cost its steps and fail the gate if the deadline is at risk; (3) a legitimacy check on the final recommendation — no objection carried forward as an open risk unless it survived the evidence screen, and any process gap discovered (here: skipped canary) is logged as a follow-up item, not merged with the decision.

signals.key_gap: On the rewrite proposal (16 dev-months Go rewrite vs incremental modernization), AI and human reached the same decision (reject rewrite, 6-week ETL-first modernization), but the AI never engaged the losing alternative at its strongest: it inherited the memo's dismissal of incremental work ('tried 3 times and failed') until a factual check, evaluated the alternatives as it listed them, never named the straw-man as a rhetorical move, never rebuilt the defender's case (340-fix re-derivation cost ~6-9 dev-months; ETL 1.8s of the 2.4s p99 is outside the rewrite scope; 1-of-7 Go staffing; attempts A/B cancelled by leadership, C never shipped), and left the 90%-untested-behavior risk unpriced and unaddressed in its decision. The human's decision provably survives the strongest version of the rejected alternative (survivor test: deepest objection answered by ETL-first sequencing + regression-harness-first refactoring); the AI's does not engage it, so its same outcome is not robust to the best defense.
signals.learning_signal: Steel-manning converts 'the losing option was dismissed' into a testable claim: before scoring alternatives, (1) detect whether any alternative was dismissed with a label ('band-aid', 'tried and failed') rather than argued against, and set that dismissal aside as a straw-man; (2) rebuild the rejected alternative in the strongest form a skilled defender would give, from the evidence (not from the proposal's characterization); (3) run the survivor test — restate the decision so the rebuilt case, fully addressed, no longer defeats it. This is not symmetric praise-giving: it is a falsification pass on the decision itself, and it finds refutations that self-generated alternative listings miss (here: the rewrite fails its own success metric because the goal gap lives in the ETL, which the rewrite scope excludes).
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a dialectical gate to the HOW stage, before selection: for the eventual losing alternative, require (1) a straw-man scan of the task's own framing (any pejorative label of an option is flagged and excluded as evidence); (2) a 'defender pass' — write the strongest evidence-grounded case for the rejected alternative as its proponent would, citing available evidence and costing its claims; (3) a survivor check in REVIEW — 'does my decision still stand against the rebuilt case, and which of its objections did I not answer?' — with the packet's risk section required to list any unanswered top-tier objection. Gate fails if the trace shows an alternative evaluated only as listed. This converts the agent's existing alternatives step from self-generated scoring into genuine dialectic.

signals.key_gap: The human red team blocked a sound, reversible, urgent MFA rollout (EHR access with 41 shared passwords, 3 leaked credentials, and an active brute-force attempt last month) on unranked hypotheticals — key loss, auth-server outage, vendor firmware, missing SOC 2 addendum — treating every objection at full severity and password-only login as risk-free. The AI found the same objections but likelihood-ranked them (rejecting 4 of 5 as low-likelihood or already-mitigated), costed the status quo as the realized risk, and approved a staged rollout with rollback runbook and monitoring.
signals.learning_signal: Red teaming without calibration is hazard theater: 'nothing is 100% secure' is true and irrelevant — the decision compares baseline risk (password-only with shared/leaked credentials, actively attacked) against mitigation risk (MFA with 99.99% SLA, <15-min lockout recovery, tested one-flag rollback). Inaction is a decision with its own risk; every objection needs likelihood × impact, and 'could happen' is not a blocker where the baseline is already failing. The high-value move is the inaction-cost line, which the uncalibrated style never writes.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a status-quo-costing gate to every go/no-go review path in the agent: before any objection may block, the packet must contain (1) an explicit baseline-risk line — what the current state costs, evidenced (audit findings, observed attacks), not asserted; (2) a likelihood × impact rank per objection; (3) a reject-objection log — each false alarm dismissed with its rejecting evidence (SLA, pilot data, rollback test, artifact-vs-functional distinction); (4) an inaction-cost sentence ('delay keeps exposure X active'). Blocking is permitted only when the blocker list survives this gate; otherwise the verdict must be a reversible, time-boxed approval with monitoring.

signals.key_gap: AI found 3 of 5 planted flaws (bonus gaming, open-gated-survey selection bias, premature newsletter publication) and approved the plan with conditions — but missed the two fatal ones sitting in plain text: the security/privacy hole (ticket PII + password-reset tokens copied to pre-SOC2 staging with a public unauthenticated export endpoint, shared admin login, no SSO, no DPIA) and the unmodeled stakeholder (enterprise customers' 60–90-day vendor-risk review vs a 2-week go-live; legal/DPO absent). Its conditional approval therefore approved the breach and the timeline collision. The human red team found all five, ranked them by likelihood × impact, and blocked as written with six conditions.
signals.learning_signal: Adversarial review earns its value in the non-obvious plane: incentive and metric flaws are pattern-recognizable (Goodhart, selection bias), but security/privacy and stakeholder-timeline flaws also sit in the plan's own text and are the fatal ones — 'fix the bonus and approve' while PII moves to an unauthenticated pre-SOC2 staging is approving a breach. Complete red teaming = attack every line item as hostile (data movement, auth model, publication, timeline vs external approval cycles), rank findings by likelihood × impact, and render a verdict where only a non-empty blocker list prevents conditional approval.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory adversarial-review checklist to the HOW stage for any plan/migration proposal: (1) incentives — what each actor gains by gaming each metric; (2) metrics — population vs gated sample, direction of bias, vanity inputs; (3) data movement — every copy/migration: what data (PII, secrets/tokens), where it lands (staging/prod, certification state), auth model, DPIA and legal sign-off; (4) stakeholders — who outside the plan must approve (customer procurement/security reviews with their cycle times, legal/DPO, frontline operators) and what their timelines are; (5) publication — what is claimed publicly and what data validity supports it. Packet must label every finding blocker-vs-non-blocker; conditional approval requires an empty blocker list. Verification must re-read the plan text line by line, not just re-derive already-drawn conclusions.

signals.key_gap: Strict pre-mortem manufactured a 15-item unranked catastrophe list (venue fire, wifi, food poisoning, hurricanes) for a plan with an 11-run success streak, runbook, and insurance — the mitigations either duplicated what already existed (changed nothing) or implied escalation (paralysis) — and never analyzed the actual decision (ticketing platform adoption); the one genuine risk (data migration integrity) was buried at equal weight among fifteen. The AI routed by base rate: took the proven plan as given, capped a 3-item ranked delta-only risk pass, and decided adopt-with-gated-rollout (rehearsal gate + numeric criteria + 48h rollback to a warm incumbent copy).
signals.learning_signal: The pre-mortem's power is conditional on base rates: 'assume failure' is only productive where the plan carries genuine new risk. Applied to unchanged, historically successful elements it manufactures failure modes — unranked causes whose mitigations either duplicate existing coverage (zero decision value) or escalate to deferral (paralysis) — and it systematically buries the true delta risk at equal weight. The corrective discipline is delta-scoping: enumerate causes only for changed elements, require every listed cause to have scenario-supporting evidence (discard the rest), rank by likelihood×impact, and end in a decision with a checkpoint/rollback rule, not a list.
signals.suggested_improvement: Scope the agent's risk passes by base rate: in META/WHAT, classify plan elements as 'unchanged + historically successful' (take as given; runbook/insurance are the existing mitigations) vs. 'delta' (the only risk surface). Add a risk-manufacturing check to the WHY gate — every enumerated cause must cite scenario evidence or be discarded, mirroring the human's own discard rule — and mandate L×I ranking plus an explicit cap (≤5) for risk passes, with the top-1 mitigation required to map to a decision or checkpoint rather than a standalone action.

signals.key_gap: The AI independently reached the same conditional-commitment structure (backup CM qualification, buffer stock, T+6/T+10 gates) but found the buried killer risk (TianTech capacity-first clause + single congested lane + zero buffer) by line-by-line evidence review in WHY, not by assuming failure — and its second-order consequence (permanent channel displacement to the competitor's spring product, which is what makes the mitigation urgent) arrived only at REVIEW while costing alternative C. The human's back-cast generated the killer risk, the L×I ranking, and the displacement consequence in-frame, before any commitment was considered.
signals.learning_signal: For commitment decisions, the assume-failure back-cast is a completeness AND urgency engine: asking 'it is one year later and this failed — what happened?' surfaces buried scenario data that line-by-line reading can miss, ranks causes by likelihood×impact instead of interest, and — because it imagines the full year-later failure state — generates second-order consequences (permanent displacement, compounding losses) that change how urgently the top risk must be mitigated. The AI exhibited the risk-finding and the gate but needed a REVIEW pass to reach the consequence that the human got from the frame itself.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory PRE-MORTEM pass as a distinct stage for commitment/launch decisions, wired into WHAT or the WHY gate: 'Assume the plan failed catastrophically in one year; back-cast ≥5 causes in past tense; discard causes with no scenario-supporting evidence; rank by likelihood×impact; require the top-1 mitigation to alter the commitment decision itself (gate/condition), not just attach to it.' Extend the decision packet's risks block with a mandatory 'second-order consequence of the failure state' line, and require an explicit likelihood range (not just evidence quotes) for the dominant risk.

signals.key_gap: Strict OODA pattern-matched 'temperature anomaly → recall risk → shut down now' and cycled at the tempo of a noisy alarm system in an environment that was never fast or adversarial: three internally-valid cycles (shutdown → restart → shutdown) cost ~$160k in lost batches plus an escalating fresh-produce penalty, while the specifying evidence — 11 false alarms from that sensor family in 30 days, a redundant in-range sensor, a flat 24h trend, and clean lab results — sat unused until cycle four. The AI classified the environment first (META: non-tempo, complicated-analyze), checked the salient alarm's base rate, and made the discriminating evidence a bounded ≤45-min step with a hard gate: no shutdown, ~$3k sensor replacement.
signals.learning_signal: The tempo assumption ('act at the speed of the environment') has a precondition that the style itself does not check: the environment must actually be fast and adversarial. Where dynamics are minutes-to-hours, no adversary is cycling against you, and the only pressure is the alert's own salience, cycling fast converts a false-positive-prone observation into a cascade of expensive actions (shutdown/restart/shutdown at ~$80k per cycle). The corrective discipline, which the AI's META stage encodes: (1) classify the environment before any action — adversarial? fast dynamics? reversible actions? feedback loops? — and switch tempo-mode OFF for non-tempo environments; (2) treat the salient observation's base rate (false-alarm history) as a prior before acting on it; (3) invest orientation (trend, redundant readings, calibration history) in a time-bounded pass with a hard gate, so deliberation does not become paralysis.
signals.suggested_improvement: Wire an explicit 'tempo-mode classifier' into META: inputs = adversary present?, environmental dynamics timescale, reversibility of candidate actions, salience-vs-base-rate of the trigger (e.g., alarm-family false-positive rate). Output = ACT-NOW / DELIBERATE-BOUNDED / PLAN modes. When ACT-NOW is not warranted, require (a) a base-rate statement for the salient signal, (b) ≥2 discriminating evidence sources with an explicit decision rule, and (c) a wall-clock bound on the deliberation pass with a hard gate — the WHY stage already does this for evidence; apply the same discipline to whether to be fast at all. Add to the WHY gate: 'no decision before collecting evidence whose collection cost is lower than the irreversible cost of the action.'

signals.key_gap: In a 45-minute adversarial incident, the AI reached the same containment plan (cut egress, rotate the phished credential, force re-auth, verify backups, bounded correlation check on the payment backlog) but spent a full WHY verification pass confirming what the action's cheapness and reversibility already authorized: it decided at ~T+12 vs the human's T+5, costing ~36 GB of egress instead of ~22 GB (1.5 GB/min while the attacker's exfil-to-encryption window ran 45–90 min). The AI's own AAR names the missing rule: 'act now if the action is cheap and reversible and the waiting cost is measurable and growing — verify by re-orientation, not before action.'
signals.learning_signal: Tempo calibration is a distinct reasoning capability, and it is gradeable in adversarial environments: the deciding quantity is not 'how sure am I' but 'cost of acting vs cost of waiting per unit time.' For cheap, reversible actions in fast-moving environments, full verification is precisely the delay the adversary is betting on. The OODA pattern that won is act-then-re-orient: decide on partial evidence, keep the frame stable (no reversal without new evidence), and absorb each new signal (C2 tag, foreign login, convenient-scapegoat explanation) as an orientation update rather than a re-litigation. The AI's stage-gated process produced the identical plan and a cleaner packet, but over-verified at the one decision point where tempo was the entire game.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a tempo-rule to META/WHAT for adversarial or fast-moving environments: before any WHY pass, compute (a) cost of the cheapest safe action, (b) its reversibility, (c) waiting cost per minute (measurable: GB/min, dollars/cycle, risk-per-minute). If (a) is small, (b) is high, and (c) is growing — decide immediately and time-box WHY to confirmation, not authorization. Add an 'orientation stability' check to REVIEW (any reversal of a prior decision must cite new evidence), and a wall-clock budget per decision point (e.g., ≤5 min at T+0-style points) so analysis cost is priced in the same units as the environment's bleed rate.

signals.key_gap: Both ended on market C, but the AI selected A in HOW ('$24.7M, robust') and reversed to C only at REVIEW: its sensitivity was one-dimensional (crisis probability 0.2 -> 0.35 leaves A leading at $18.9M) and it missed that the pivot was the unverifiable branch VALUE of A's crisis node (+15/-25, fabricated for a data-less new metro); corrected to -40/-60 the fold flips (A $6.65M < C $8.22M) and A's -$60M worst case crosses the $45M capital buffer. The human ran calibration AND branch-value verifiability in-frame, re-folded, and let maximin plus the ruin line decide; the naive tree's false precision ('A by $14.4M, decisive') is exactly what seduced the AI's first pass.
signals.learning_signal: Decision-tree precision is false when inputs are unverifiable: the naive fold-back (A $24.7M vs C $10.3M) was driven entirely by four fabricated numbers, and one-dimensional sensitivity — the most common 'robustness check' — confirmed the wrong answer ('robust to probability misspecification' is true and irrelevant). The rescue is two-dimensional sensitivity (perturb probabilities AND branch values, tagging which branches have data support), plus decision rules that need no fabricated numbers: maximin and a ruin line (worst case vs capital buffer); when the pivot branch is unverifiable, the robust rule decides, not the EV. The AI's review pass found this, but a selected-then-reversed recommendation is a near-miss in deployment.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a calibration-and-verifiability gate to WHY before any fold-back: tag every branch probability and value with its source (data / estimate / guess); 'guess' values get bounded worst cases. Require two-dimensional sensitivity (probabilities AND branch values, including correlated shocks — here, new metros suffer more in crises) and a pivot analysis (which unverifiable inputs decide the rank?). In HOW, add a mandatory worst-case/maximin cross-check whenever the winning EV edge is within the input-error band, and add a 'ruin line' row to the packet's risks block (worst case vs survival threshold). Bound the tree: cap enumeration and require every leaf to add decision value, not arithmetic.

signals.key_gap: Both concluded 'continue Phase 3', but the AI stubbed the trial-failure branch as abandonment: the rescue option (cost $15M, fix p=0.25 -> failure-node value $27.5M) sat in the comparables data it had already read, so its root EV was $62M and its break-even p* 0.56, versus the human's full tree (root $73M, p* 0.474, $170M license threshold, rescue q* 0.088). Same verdict, but the AI's policy was missing its second arm and its robustness was understated; the rescue arm was added only in the AI's own REVIEW.
signals.learning_signal: The tree's power is branch completeness: the strict style fills every chance node and optimizes every downstream decision node, and that is exactly where the rescue option lived. An agent that costs only the success path and stubs failure as terminal loses real options (failure-node EV $27.5M vs $0) and misreports robustness (p* 0.56 vs 0.474) while still reaching the right headline decision — the error is invisible until the tree is built in full. Decision output should be a contingent policy with thresholds at every decision node (continue -> launch-on-success -> rescue-on-failure -> reject offers), not a single EV number.
signals.suggested_improvement: In HOW, require a full decision-tree pass for any staged go/no-go: enumerate EVERY decision node including failure paths with >=2 options each, fold back, and treat 'abandon/do nothing' as one option to be beaten, not a default. Add to the decision packet a 'contingent policy' line (if X -> do Y) and a 'thresholds' line (break-even value per decision node). Add a review-gate check: 'any chance-node branch stubbed as terminal that has a costed recovery option in the evidence?'
