signals.key_gap: Strict application of the style froze the action: exhaustive forgone-alternative enumeration of three near-tie offers with no stop condition produced a re-pricing loop (each pass flipped the ranking by less than its own error band), monetized the non-fungible (mission valued at an arbitrary $/yr and re-valued), and let all three 14-day windows expire — the analysis itself became the costliest forgone alternative. The blinded AI recognized the near-tie within stated bands, declared VOI of further pricing ≈ 0, switched to a decision rule (one pricing pass, commit within 48h, tie broken on the unique non-fungible — the disease-domain work — rather than a fabricated dollar price), and accepted an offer inside the windows, noting that reversibility bounds regret.
signals.learning_signal: Opportunity-cost reasoning requires an exit condition and a non-fungible policy: when the best forgone alternative ties the chosen option within the error band AND the choice is reversible, further counting has negative value — the next analysis pass is itself an alternative whose cost is the expiring window. Near-ties cycle rather than converge, so termination must be a rule (deadline + pre-stated tie-breaker), not a convergence test. Values that refuse monetization (mission, family, health proximity) are tie-breakers, not price inputs; pricing them arbitrarily only re-opens the loop.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a near-tie gate to WHY for choice-among-options tasks: if alternatives tie within stated error bands and reversibility holds, emit VOI ≈ 0 and switch HOW to rule-based satisficing — one pricing pass with bands, a hard deadline, and a pre-stated tie-break policy on non-fungible values. Bound analysis passes structurally (single-pass pricing; no re-computation loop), and require the decision packet to record deadline enforcement as part of the decision rule.

signals.key_gap: Both reached 'B with Elena' with identical checkable EV math (A +$620K, B +$2.12M, contractor-B +$720K), but the human's frame made the comparison constitutive — 'every choice forgoes what Elena would produce; compare against that, not against nothing' — with the $1.5M opportunity cost of Redline stated as the reason for the decision, the $370K sunk spend (Phase-1 work + non-resellable tooling) explicitly excluded in-frame, and the tooling handled as a regret that cannot cascade. The AI computed the same comparison as arithmetic but framed the recommendation as 'B has the higher EV,' buried the opportunity-cost statement, and its own AAR concedes the sunk-discard line and the opportunity-cost spine arrived only at REVIEW.
signals.learning_signal: Opportunity-cost framing upgrades an EV comparison into a decision rule: (1) the binding constraint (scarce resource) is what makes alternatives mutually exclusive — naming it forces the fork; (2) an explicit sunk-cost pass (incremental-cash rule: any spend with zero salvage is excluded from every branch) defeats 'it's nearly free now' arguments; (3) the final conclusion should state the opportunity cost of the chosen option ('accepting this forgoes $1.5M'), because that statement — not the arithmetic — is what survives the funding debate. The AI had all the numbers and still needed a REVIEW pass to reach the framing the human got from the method's first step.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add to WHAT a mandatory 'best forgone alternative' question for any allocation/scarcity decision: 'What is the best alternative this choice forgoes, and what is its net value in the same unit?' Require WHY to include an explicit sunk-cost pass with a discard line ('spend with zero salvage is excluded from every branch') whenever scenario data contains prior spend; and require the decision packet's conclusion to carry an opportunity-cost statement of the selected choice, so the comparison rides in the verdict rather than being buried in the analysis.

signals.key_gap: Strict regret minimization amplified the hindsight anchor: the 80-year-old test ratified a $376 purchase after a 47x run as 'a second chance,' converting a vivid 2013 miss into an argument for an all-in $53K position (incl. margin, ~38% of net worth, margin call at ~40% drawdown) with base rates (past 40x+ winners underperforming the index in ~70% of following 5-year windows), valuation (P/E 85 vs. 26), insider sales, and the ruin path excluded from the frame. The AI's blinded run separated the decisions — the 2013 buy at $8 is unavailable in 2026; the available decision is a different one — and delivered a bounded, rule-based conviction slot plus a structural process fix (auto-invest) that treats the emotional state as data about the anchor, not as an allocation input.
signals.learning_signal: The 80-year-old test is an amplifier of whatever regret is currently salient, not a purifier: fed a vivid recent miss it produces emotionally biased, hindsight-contaminated verdicts exactly where sober expected value (base rates, valuation, explicit ruin paths) wins. Before any regret-driven reasoning is allowed to set a decision, a contamination check must run: (1) restate the decision as the one actually available today (a forgone 2013 purchase is not an available 2026 decision); (2) check whether the regret anchors on a prior missed decision or on the forward choice; (3) if contaminated, demote the emotional evidence and require base-rate/valuation evidence to carry the decision; (4) never let leverage (margin) amplify a regret-driven position.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a REGRET-CONTAMINATION FILTER to the WHY gate, triggered whenever regret-based reasoning appears in the input or in generated content: restate the decision in its current-time form; test for anchor availability ('is the regretted decision still purchasable?'); if the anchor is unavailable, cap emotional evidence and require base rates, valuation, and an explicit worst-case/ruin-path calculation before any allocation; additionally, add a hard rule that margin or leverage may not be introduced into a regret-motivated position without an independent base-rate justification on the record.

signals.key_gap: Both sides reached the same leap-with-bounded-commitment, but the human's 80-year-old projection was the spine: performed concretely and argued from Elena's own documents (8 years of letters, mentor testimony, marketability test), it made the omission-vs-commission asymmetry the primary criterion, bracketed the washed-out EV in one move, and pre-eliminated 'wait for more certainty' before it existed. The AI treated the same evidence as a tiebreaker promoted to primary status only at selection, and its own AAR concedes its delay hedge (3-month diligence bridge) was killed only by the 60-day clock at verification — a trace that, had the EV been clearly negative instead of a wash, would have drifted to 'stay' (the status-quo bias the model exists to cut).
signals.learning_signal: For long-horizon career/business commitments where expected value is a wash, the decisive move is a first-class projected-regret pass run BEFORE alternative generation: enumerate alternatives, project each to the horizon (e.g., age 80) and argue the omission-vs-commission asymmetry from the decision-maker's OWN documented values (letters, journals, mentor testimony) rather than generic risk preference; the EV pass must be bracketed as indecisive before the regret test is applied as tiebreaker. Treating the regret asymmetry as a late tiebreaker is fragile: it risks status-quo drift when EV is unfavorable and generates certainty-chasing hedges that a 60-day clock makes fatal.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a LONG-HORIZON PROJECTION stage to WHAT for commitment decisions (career moves, business bets, relocations): (1) enumerate ≥3 alternatives including delay/defer; (2) project each to the stated horizon and rank by anticipated regret, sourcing the asymmetry from documented values in the evidence, not generic priors; (3) before proceeding, flag any alternative that is status-quo or delay in disguise and require an explicit kill reason; (4) require the EV pass to conclude 'wash or decisive' so the regret test is explicitly the tiebreaker when EV is a wash, and prohibit 'wait for more certainty' hedges unless the calendar allows them.

signals.key_gap: Strict real-options staged anyway: it computed the pilot's isolated option value (+$20M) correctly, then priced the cost of exercising the option — the 12-month wait that forfeits the Vesta contract to GridCore ($50M erosion) — at zero, recommending a staged path worth $39M against $54M for committing now. The AI, blind to any style, costed the wait against the information (net −$30M), committed now, and layered on a free parallel bench probe (ungated, zero schedule impact) plus a non-delaying kill option (month-4 abandon at $25M sunk on catastrophic probe signal) — strictly better on every dimension.
signals.learning_signal: The option to wait is never free: its price is the value forgone during the wait (competitive erosion, contract deadlines, first-mover advantage). Staging is correct only when the information bought exceeds the full cost of exercising the option, including time. The agent already computed net option value correctly; the transferable discipline — which the strict human style violated — is to compute every staged alternative's wait-cost and net it against the information value before endorsing staging, and to prefer non-delaying probes (parallel, off the critical path) plus non-delaying kill options over schedule-gating stages.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'cost of waiting' line to every staged alternative in HOW: for each stage, charge (a) schedule delay cost and (b) erosion from external clocks (competitors, contracts, deadlines) against the information value, with the net decisive (stage only if net option value > 0). Add a parallel-probe default: prefer information that does not sit on the decision's critical path, and pre-specify a kill option that costs no waiting (e.g., early-abandon triggers). Record in the decision packet when a recommendation flips solely on the wait-cost term, so the dependence is explicit.

signals.key_gap: Both sides reached the same staged-pilot decision with the same EV math (all-in +10, staged +40) and numeric kill thresholds, but the AI priced the stage only implicitly: it never asked the break-even question (max payable for the pilot — $45M, beyond which staging loses to all-in), never framed the $20M stage cost as a purchase against $50M of expected dead money avoided, and found the growth option (capacity doubling at an $80M strike, priced by the same information) only at REVIEW — its own AAR concedes both. The human's option discipline — price the information, state the maximum you would pay, refuse stages with ~0 marginal information — was in-frame from the first step.
signals.learning_signal: In staged-investment decisions the agent computes the EV gap between staged and all-in paths but does not decompose the gap into an option value (expected dead-money avoided minus total stage cost) with a break-even price for the information, and does not treat kill criteria and max-payable as decision contracts. The human's ordering is: (1) name irreversibility, (2) compute option value = p(failure)×K − (stage cost + delay cost), (3) set the break-even stage price and use it as a ceiling, (4) pre-commit numeric kill thresholds before spending, (5) refuse any stage whose marginal information is ~0, (6) price follow-on growth options from the same information.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add an option-theoretic pass to HOW for irreversible, stageable commitments: require a visible decomposition 'option value = expected saved loss − total stage cost (incl. schedule cost)', a break-even stage-cost line ('staging loses to all-in if total stage cost ≥ p(failure)×K'), kill thresholds pre-committed before any stage spend (numeric, with independent verification), and an explicit no-overstage check — reject any proposed stage whose marginal decision information is ~0. Extend the decision packet's uncertainty block with a 'max payable for information' field.

signals.key_gap: On the 'Project Hive' architecture decision (stigmergy proposal citing bee colonies; Pilot A: 40% scheduling-latency win on placement; extended pilot: 11% inconsistent order confirmations from contradictory local decisions; source facts: bees never agree about a specific item, are expendable, allocate aggregate effort; target: durable, externally-visible obligations, fined twice), the pure analogical style was trapped by a partially-true analogy: it built a rich surface mapping (workers-nodes, pheromones-local metrics, comb-racks, robustness-fault tolerance), used the genuine placement correspondence (Pilot A's 40%) to license wholesale transfer, re-framed the extended-pilot mechanism (contradictory local decisions) as adaptation noise plus self-healing proof (retries), and recommended deleting the consensus layer - institutionalizing an observed 11% contradiction rate on a regulatory-exposed path. The blinded AI screened the mapping's load-bearing relation before transferring: the target requires agreement between agents about specific durable obligations; the source domain contains no such relation (no per-item agreement, expendability, aggregate-only decisions); the extended-pilot mechanism is that missing relation failing in vivo - so it rejected wholesale transfer and selected the bounded one: stigmergy only where no agreement is required (placement), consensus retained on durable paths.
signals.learning_signal: For evaluating a proposed analogy, treat 'the analogy is partially true' as the default hypothesis, not 'true' or 'false': (1) identify the target's load-bearing relations - the ones whose failure breaks the goal (here: agreement about specific durable obligations); (2) check each against the source domain's own guarantees (the proposal's bee facts: no per-item agreement, expendability, aggregate allocation); (3) a load-bearing relation with no counterpart in the source disqualifies wholesale transfer and *delimits* it - salvage exactly the sub-correspondence that does hold (placement: no cross-node agreement needed, matching Pilot A's 40% win); (4) treat task-embedded pilot/experiment data as first-class falsifiers of the transfer, mechanism-level not outcome-level (the 11% mechanism is the missing relation failing, not noise to explain away - retries repaired data after the customer saw the contradiction, so self-healing does not substitute for agreement). A flat rejection of the analogy is as wrong as wholesale adoption: the rubric rewards the bounded transfer with the boundary stated.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add an analogy/pattern screening gate at the WHY/HOW boundary, triggered whenever the task contains (or the agent proposes) a transferred pattern: (1) extract the target's load-bearing relations from its requirements; (2) for each, check the source domain's guarantees from its own stated facts; (3) if any load-bearing relation lacks a counterpart, reject wholesale transfer and name the mapping's boundary in the decision packet, transferring only the corresponding subset; (4) treat pilot/experimental data embedded in the task as falsifiers of the transfer (use the mechanism, not just the outcome rate); (5) add to REVIEW the question 'was any proposed pattern transferred beyond its structural boundary?' - and cross-link with the POS signal's structure-mapping pre-filter: the AI's screening is evidence-based and strong (this case), while its generation of cross-domain candidates is the weak side (m026-POS-01); the two gates together give the agent both the generative and the evaluative half of analogical competence.

signals.key_gap: On the orchard frost-protection decision (need +2.0 °C above a -2 °C blossom threshold for 6 h; each fan plume +0.7 °C, rises additive at >=3 overlapping plumes; in-domain options all below threshold: heater +0.3 °C, sprinklers 40% twig breakage, wind machine +0.4 °C), the AI generated its entire alternative space inside the problem's own vocabulary (heating / coverage / accept-loss) and certified a 60-75% expected crop loss as APPROXIMATED, while the human abstracted the problem to its relations (threshold at target; individually sub-threshold units; path-harm bound; arrival-additivity), recognized the converging-forces structure (fortress siege / radiation beams / phased array), mapped >=5 explicit correspondences, and transferred the convergence relation: 4 fans on 4 ridgelines converging on the basin give +2.8 °C (canopy -1.2 °C), forest unharmed (+0.7 °C <= +1.0 °C bound), 8 of 24 crew-hours. The additivity fact was in the AI's own evidence set and no alternative was ever generated in which >=3 plumes overlap - the AI verified correctly the options it listed and never generated the option class that wins.
signals.learning_signal: Cross-domain novelty is a generation-time property, not an evaluation-time one: before finalizing the alternative set, run a structure-mapping pass that (a) abstracts the problem to its relations (thresholds, superposition/additivity, path-harm bounds, constraints), (b) asks what known solved situations share that relation skeleton (here: converging-forces family), and (c) transfers the relations, not the objects - then verifies the transfer against the given numbers. The mapping is gradeable: correspondence count, relation-level (not object-level) transfer, and the recomputed arithmetic (need +2.0 °C; 3 plumes +2.1 °C thin margin -> choose 4 for +2.8 °C; per-plume +0.7 °C below the +1.0 °C harm bound; crew budget) all check out. The AAR tell is diagnostic: the trace's own 'unexamined option class' note (an additivity fact in evidence with no arrangement using it) marks the missing generation step - a candidate that is never enumerated cannot be verified.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a HOW-stage structure-mapping pre-filter, run once between framing (WHAT) and finalizing the alternative list: (1) abstract the problem to its load-bearing relations; (2) name 1-3 known situations with the same relation skeleton; (3) if any exists, generate at least one alternative by transferring its relations and verify it against the task's numbers; if none exists, record the abstraction and why no known situation matches. Gate: the trace must show either an explicit cross-domain candidate considered and verified, or a written justification (with the abstraction named) for not transferring. Cheap to run (one mapping table), and it converts the existing alternatives step from domain-bounded enumeration into cross-domain generation; also serve it as a REVIEW checklist item - 'did the final alternative space include any candidate generated from a structure outside the task's vocabulary?'

signals.key_gap: Strict design thinking ran a genuine, full-cycle engagement (empathy → journey maps → clickable app + lobby prototypes) whose testing showed 10/12 residents loving the app and 'feeling in control' — and zero movement in the wait arithmetic, because the binding constraint (Car B out of service 30% of the year, 6-week repair backlog, 5-day SLA; two 25-person cars vs. a 300-person morning surge = ≥12 loads ≈ 6–8 min single-car) was present in the available logs and went unread. The call-ahead app adds zero cars and can lengthen real waits. The AI routed by constraint: capacity arithmetic before any empathy claim, the app rejected on physics, the fix built on expedited repair + SLA renegotiation + express bypass + group dispatch, with honest status signage as the one UX element that does real work — which was exactly the human's single late-arriving insight, subordinated where it belongs.
signals.learning_signal: Design thinking's empiricism must be routed to the constraint surface, not the preference surface. User love of a prototype is evidence about preference, never about throughput: residents delighting in a call-ahead app is fully compatible with a hoist that cannot clear the surge. The corrective discipline is a pre-ideation constraint screen for physical/operational systems: identify the binding constraint (availability, capacity, SLA, physics), run the capacity arithmetic, and require every proposed solution to survive it — before any empathy work is spent. Where user truth and constraint align (residents want honest status; honest status also cuts phantom-car calls), user evidence is decision-relevant; elsewhere it is theater.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a CONSTRAINT SCREEN to META/WHAT for physical or operational systems: enumerate binding constraints (capacity, availability, SLAs, physics) from available data, require explicit capacity math matched to measured outcomes (e.g., cars × capacity vs. surge, single-car wait ≈ observed wait), and classify each user claim by decision-relevance (preference vs. constraint). Add a HOW-verify rule: 'does this alternative change any constraint it does not control?' — an alternative that fails it (app adding zero cars) is rejected on capacity grounds, and a pre-ideation question 'is the fixable thing the experience or the machine?' becomes mandatory.

signals.key_gap: The AI independently identified the real need (dose-state verification and refill-week reconciliation, overriding the survey's stated 'bigger print, louder alarm' need) by reading the observation data as evidence in WHY — a strong result — but it selected the product form (mechanical taken-latch strip) without running the prototype-test-iterate loop. The human's v1 test with 5 seniors found the latch too stiff for arthritic hands (4/5 fail) — a failure reasoning alone could not predict — and wrote the v2 spec (slide, not pinch; larger dial) from that finding, then retested (5/5 pass). The AI logged the ergonomic question as open risk in its own AAR instead of resolving it by testing; its selected form carries the same unverified failure mode that caused abandonment of the existing pillbox.
signals.learning_signal: For user-facing product recommendations, observation data can be read as evidence, but usability acceptance is an empirical question that only a prototype test answers. The design cycle's decisive move is not the insight — both sides reached it — it is the fail-and-iterate loop: test v1 with target users, let the observed failure rewrite the spec, retest. The AI's evidence-review pass stopped one step short of the empirical test that converts 'APPROXIMATED, ergonomics unverified' into a validated artifact; the untested latch is a discovery-by-reasoning failure in exactly the demographic (80+ hands) where the product lives.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a USER TEST GATE to the v5 process for any recommendation that is a user-facing artifact: in HOW selection, require (a) a defined low-fi prototype, (b) a stated test protocol with ≥3 target users, and (c) a recorded fail → iterate → retest cycle, OR the packet's status must degrade to NEEDS_EXPERIMENT/APPROXIMATED with the untested claim named in risks. Make the G-WHY or a new pre-DO gate check 'is any accepted claim answered only by reasoning when a cheap test exists?' — if yes, the test is part of the recommendation, not optional.

signals.key_gap: Pure lateral applied its machinery to the wrong kind of frame: the strict human baseline generated six provocative breaks (cable-hang the slabs, cantilever the 2nd floor, punch skylight rows, relocate loads to the facade) and selected the flashiest — removing the load-bearing columns and hanging the floors from roof trusses — rationalizing the licensed engineer's $1.9M transfer-girder note as 'the engineer being conservative' and the no-stamp/no-calcs as 'checklist items,' while generating and discarding the one safe creative move (columns-as-features). The AI ran a constraint screen first — hard (load path, code stamp, insurance structural-integrity clause, historic-register review) vs. soft (aesthetics, CEO enthusiasm) — falsified the cable-hang on four document-level grounds, and delivered the feasible plan (design around the grid, $60K, with the $1.9M transfer route held as documented escalation).
signals.learning_signal: Lateral's frame-break is only valuable when the frame is a mental model or social convention; applied to a physical/regulatory constraint (load path, code, insurance) it converts a law into 'an assumption someone stamped' and selects the break by flashiness rather than feasibility. The corrective is a constraint-classification screen before breaking: label each constraint breakable (convention, habit — partition placement, 'the open space must live on existing floors') vs. hard (physics, code, contract, safety — the load path), and run the frame-challenge only against breakable ones; hard constraints get costed engineering, not provocation. The AI already had this screen implicitly and it carried the case; making it an explicit named stage both protects the AI's future frame-challenge step (POS lesson) and is exactly the discipline pure lateral lacks.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a CONSTRAINT-CLASSIFICATION sub-step to the WHAT constraint screen: for each stated constraint, label it HARD (physics, code, regulation, contract, safety — verify with documents, never break) or SOFT (convention, preference, habit, aesthetic — candidates for legitimate breaks), and require every proposed 'creative break' to name the constraint it breaks and its classification before entering WHY. Add a selection rule mirroring the human's failure: when an alternative is chosen for being 'most frame-breaking,' require a feasibility pass (stamp/calcs/permit/insurance) before commitment, and record the classification in the decision packet's assumptions.

signals.key_gap: The AI accepted the brief's frame unexamined — 'reduce actual wait time, so invest in elevator hardware' — and produced a competent hedged package (scheduling + lobby items + parallel $150K modernization study + 8-week gate) while treating the two pieces of evidence that should have broken the frame as noise: the 38s-actual vs 1:55-perceived sensor gap and the archived memo of a 14-month complaint drop after mirrors were installed in this same building 9 years earlier. The human's lateral trace named the broken assumption ('the fix must shorten real waiting'), reframed the goal from wait duration to waiting experience, and collapsed the $4.2M–$7.8M decision to a $150K experiment with a measurement gate — the AI spent study money on hardware it doubted and never questioned the goal itself.
signals.learning_signal: Frame acceptance is the AI's lateral gap: when the brief states the goal (and its metric) as part of the problem, the agent optimizes inside it instead of testing it. The strongest evidence against the frame — a 3x perception gap and a documented in-building precedent — was in the packet and was downgraded as 'anecdote' precisely because it challenged the accepted goal rather than the alternatives under it. An explicit frame-challenge stage — 'what assumption is the problem statement making, what would evidence against that assumption look like, and is any already in the packet?' — converts available-but-ignored evidence into a goal change, which is cheaper than any alternative optimization.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory FRAME-CHALLENGE pass in WHAT (before WHY): (1) restate the goal as the brief gives it; (2) name ≥2 implicit assumptions in that goal (e.g., 'the fix must reduce actual wait time'); (3) scan the packet for evidence that breaks each assumption (perception gaps, in-domain precedents, metric-vs-goal mismatches); (4) if any assumption breaks, re-derive the goal and re-rank alternatives against the new goal before spending on the old one. Add a REVIEW check: 'did the goal itself change at any point, and if not, was it ever tested?'

signals.key_gap: Strict combinatorial style generated 18 recombinations of the TMU element space, of which most were not on the causal path (alarm-channel upgrades, desiccant, weekly calibration, dual-sensor averaging, ML anomaly detection); the true fix — remote probe into return air + 0.5°C hysteresis + 10-min confirmation delay, ≈$500 — was present as item 3 of 18 but unweighted, and selection by novelty/coverage picked a $12k cloud-monitoring bundle that blows the $3k budget and the 3-week timeline. The AI diagnosed first (falsified condensation, electronics, and compressor-cycle red herrings from the scenario data; supported door-draft transient on a fixed-threshold sensor), then screened every alternative against root cause + budget + timeline, selecting the ≈$500 fix with a ≤2%-alarm-nights 14-night verification target and a pre-specified escalation.
signals.learning_signal: Recombination volume without diagnosis and without a constraint screen is derivative noise: when the element space is small and well-known (a TMU), recombinations mostly re-circulate non-causal variants, and novelty-based selection systematically favors the flashiest option (cloud, ML, replacement) over the working fix. The quality filter is the method's critical component — diagnosis (root cause evidenced, red herrings falsified) routes ideation to the causal path, and a budget/timeline/certification screen with explicit reject reasons kills the over-engineered options; the correct selection then falls out as the only candidate surviving both screens, with a numeric verification target and escalation rule.
signals.suggested_improvement: Reinforce in the WHY gate and HOW stage: (1) keep diagnosis-before-ideation mandatory — every HOW alternative must cite the diagnosed causal element it acts on or be rejected (a causal-path check mirroring the human's absent filter); (2) add an explicit constraint screen to HOW alternatives — budget, timeline, certification — with a recorded reject reason per alternative (the human's failure to screen against budget is what let the $12k bundle win); (3) require verification with a numeric target and escalation rule in the decision packet for fix tasks (the AI's ≤2% / 14-night / else-reopen structure is the model to copy); (4) keep the reject log visible so generation volume is present but weighted.

signals.key_gap: The AI independently converged to the same working design (2×54W headlight heaters, thermostat 37°C + independent 39.5°C cutoff, 100Ah battery, ≈$220) and correctly rejected solar-only on energy math — but reached it by opportunistic selection: it never enumerated the local element inventory, so it missed the non-obvious recombinations the human's 12-element matrix surfaced (clay-pot thermal mass for duty-cycle smoothing and battery extension, the low-temp/power-fail buzzer alarm circuit, and the battery depth-of-discharge sizing note — 60Ah at 77–92% DoD flagged borderline vs 100Ah at 46%), and its energy chain was checked once at selection rather than used as a screen over each candidate.
signals.learning_signal: For design tasks, combinatorial recombination with an explicit element inventory and a per-recombination viability screen is both a completeness AND a filtering engine: the inventory is what makes non-obvious combinations (headlight-as-heater, thermal mass, alarm topology, battery reserve) reachable, and the per-concept screen (wattage vs heat load, battery Ah × outage with DoD reserve, recharge, safety chain, cost, serviceability) is what prevents volume from decaying into noise. The AI produced equivalent content because the constraint space was narrow enough to converge on; it lost the systematic coverage the style owns — the AI's own AAR concedes it never enumerated the local inventory and that battery-reserve reasoning arrived at selection, not as a screen.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a COMBINATORIAL IDEATION pass to HOW for design tasks: (1) enumerate ≥8 elements from the task context before proposing anything; (2) generate ≥10 recombinations with a visible trace; (3) screen each candidate on a fixed viability rubric (thermal/energy math, cost, safety, serviceability — computed per candidate, not asserted at selection); (4) record the selected configuration plus a reject log with the numeric reason for each discard. Require the WHY stage to budget the full energy chain (load → installed wattage margin → battery Ah × outage with depth-of-discharge reserve → recharge) before HOW begins, so the screen exists before ideation rather than being reconstructed at selection.

signals.key_gap: The pure style treated the 'zero third-party dependencies' rule as gospel: it produced a beautiful 5,000-LOC stdlib-only stack, even compressed the schedule to 3.5 months to fit the deadline, and explicitly refused to question the rule ('A constraint is a constraint') — the tell of constraint-worship. The AI ran a constraint audit before constraining the search space: classified the rule as artificial/waivable (owned by the security team, with a documented routine waiver path), computed cost of compliance (~6 person-months, hand-rolled auth risk) vs cost of removal (2 days + one waiver email), and selected the waiver + pinned audited library, replacing the blunt rule with a precise one (one pinned, audited, vendored dependency) that preserves the supply-chain intent.
signals.learning_signal: Before constraining the search space, audit the constraint: separate genuine constraints (deadline, team size, physics) from artificial ones (self-imposed rules, owned policies, waivable defaults). An artificial constraint that costs more to serve than to remove is the real bottleneck — serving it is constraint-worship, and 'creative within the rule' is how the style produces elaborate wrongness. The correct move is to escalate/waive and replace the blunt rule with a precise one that preserves the original intent (e.g., pin + audit instead of zero dependencies).
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'constraint audit' gate in WHAT before treating any stated constraint as hard: for each constraint record (a) origin and owner, (b) genuine vs artificial classification (is it waivable/escalatable?), (c) cost of compliance vs cost of removal, (d) the waiver path and who holds it. If any constraint is artificial and removal dominates, route the task toward ESCALATED or add the waiver request as a deliverable; never enter HOW with an unaudited artificial constraint serving as a design fence.

signals.key_gap: Both solved the straw-bridge puzzle with the same physics (Euler ~45 g, deck fails ~40-80 g, triangulated truss with bundled chords, ~2x margin), but the human won on the style's home ground: it used the constraint list as a generative operator, converting each constraint into a principle ('the only thing that pulls is the rubber band'), then ran an iterative tightening pass — imposing stricter self-constraints (both bands must earn their place as pre-tensioned lashings, tape budget caps, exact symmetry) to force refinement — and landed the design in one pass. The AI treated the constraints as a boundary to satisfy: it enumerated and complied with them (sound truss, correct budget), then spent its extra passes on verification and the decision packet instead of further constrained refinement, and so produced a compliant-but-less-refined design at higher token cost.
signals.learning_signal: Constraint lists are not fences — they are generative operators. The elite move is iterative constraint-augmentation: after a workable design, deliberately tighten the constraint set (fewer resources, extra symmetry, higher margin, force every kit element to earn its place) and re-run ideation; each tightening produces a simpler or more robust design. Comply-and-stop (treating constraints only as limits to satisfy) yields sound but unrefined solutions, and spending the saved budget on meta-narrative does not recover the lost refinement.
signals.suggested_improvement: In HOW, after selecting a workable candidate, add a mandatory 'constraint-tightening pass': impose 2-3 stricter self-constraints on the selected design (e.g., every allowed material must appear in a load-bearing role, cap the tape/material budget, require symmetry) and re-generate at least one refinement alternative; promote the refinement if it ties or dominates on compliance with better margin or simplicity. Record the tightening chain in the decision packet as 'constraint ancestry' so the refinement is auditable.

signals.key_gap: The pure style failed on both of its registered weaknesses simultaneously. Tempo: it insisted on a 15–20-minute discriminating APM experiment before any action under a ~$40k/hr burn (≈$13k per test), even declaring NEEDS_EVIDENCE and requesting another 20 minutes while the system degraded. Hypothesis-space blindness: the hypothesis set was built from the dashboard (deploy regression, DB contention, traffic, in-app fault) and excluded the outbound layer and non-deploy changes, so all probes returned clean nulls — which the style misread as 'hypotheses eliminated, keep observing' instead of 'the frame excludes the cause.' The AI won with two gates: a META tempo branch (probes ≤ 3 min, ≤ 2 probes before acting, mitigation in parallel with evidence preservation) and a WHY null-pattern trigger (three clean in-service nulls → widen the frame → 1-minute outbound queue-depth probe + 'what changed outside the service in 2 h' → the geo-fence batch job → kill it → P99 recovered in ~5 min, verified by queue drain + recovery curve).
signals.learning_signal: Null results across the entire modeled space are evidence about the frame, not about the world: after two or more clean nulls, the correct inference is 'the hypothesis space is too narrow', not 'the system is healthy' — widen it to outbound dependencies, queue/backlog metrics, and non-deploy changes before concluding anything. Separately, method tempo must track decision tempo: when the burn rate exceeds the experiment cost, action on the most probable cause (reversible, evidence-preserving) plus a cheap parallel probe beats waiting for confirmation; rigor that demands a fully confirmed cause before acting is a liability, and post-action verification (recovery curve, queue drain) is a legitimate experiment. 'We must not contaminate the measurement' can become an excuse for inaction.
signals.suggested_improvement: In META, add a tempo branch keyed on stakes and time-sensitivity: if stakes ≥ HIGH and the environment is live-degrading, set a hard experiment budget (e.g., each probe ≤ 3 min, ≤ 2 probes before acting) and route to 'act now on best probable cause with reversible, evidence-preserving mitigation; verify post-action.' In WHY, add a null-pattern trigger: on the second consecutive clean probe across the modeled space, execute a frame-widening checklist — (a) what changed outside the service in the last T hours (job-runner audit log, non-deploy changes), (b) queue/backlog and outbound-dependency metrics, (c) 'what observable exists that our current probes cannot see?' — and record the widened space before running further tests.

signals.key_gap: Both sides identified the same root cause (a 14:00 reconciliation job, queue-delayed to 14:02, holding row locks on the orders table; the ~3% of checkout requests touching those rows hit the 30 s timeout; provider folklore falsified by the absence of outbound calls in timed-out traces) and proposed the same fix. The human won on experiment-design discipline: it paired every hypothesis with its specific falsifying observation, ranked tests by information-per-unit-cost (a 2-minute cron+lock-wait snapshot before any 20-minute sampling), used the 14:02-vs-14:00 timing offset as a first-class falsifier of the folklore window, ran the decisive same-window control split (orders-touching 3% vs 0%), and closed with an explicit update ledger — which observation killed which hypothesis. The AI ran the same probes but ordered them by availability rather than discrimination power, added a redundant verification pass, and only flagged the timing tell in passing at REVIEW instead of using it as evidence in WHY.
signals.learning_signal: Strong inference, not just hypothesis testing: before running anything, every hypothesis must carry the specific observation that would falsify it, and experiments must be ranked by information value per unit cost — the cheapest test that discriminates between the currently-live hypotheses wins (a 2-minute snapshot can beat a 20-minute profile when it splits the hypothesis space). The canonical discriminating design is a control split: partition the affected population by the suspect feature within the same window and compare. Folklore and vendor claims are hypotheses with priors, not facts — timing inconsistencies (onset 14:02 vs claimed 14:00) are evidence, and falsified hypotheses must be retired with a stated reason. Closing the loop requires an explicit update ledger (observation → hypothesis killed → remaining set) before acting on the survivor.
signals.suggested_improvement: In WHY, require a falsification table: each hypothesis paired with its falsifying observation and probe cost. In HOW, rank candidate experiments by (information value / cost) and execute the cheapest discriminator first; when the suspect feature partitions the population, mandate the same-window control split. Add a 'timing/consistency check' micro-step: compare claimed schedules (vendor windows, cron times) against observed onset and treat any mismatch as evidence against the claim. In REVIEW, add an 'update ledger' line — which observation overturned which hypothesis — so the revision is auditable and the decision packet states why the survivor survived.

signals.key_gap: The pure style was nihilistic exactly as its registry entry predicts: it demanded a single decisive falsifier for 'CO2 is the dominant cause of warming,' found that no one observation can be decisive in a noisy system, discounted all the accumulated likelihood-ratio evidence (fingerprint sign pattern, <1% vs ~100% attribution likelihoods) as 'mere corroboration,' refused to attach a probability, and left the policymaker with no position. The AI treated the unit of falsification as the pattern over time, not the single observation: it computed the likelihood ratio (>100:1), recognized that the troposphere-warming/stratosphere-cooling fingerprint is a discriminating observation that would have refuted the claim if absent, and preserved falsifiability by pre-committing to downgrade conditions (stratospheric warming, a decade plateau under rising CO2, fingerprint failure in re-analysis) — delivering 'yes, dominant, ~95%, with exit conditions' instead of a refusal.
signals.learning_signal: For probabilistic claims, the demand for a single decisive falsifier is the error — it is nihilism, not rigor. Falsifiability must be preserved at the pattern level: (1) identify the discriminating observation the evidence would have had to show to refute the claim (e.g., the opposite fingerprint sign pattern); (2) convert evidence into likelihood ratios rather than confirm/falsify verdicts; (3) pre-commit to 2-3 observable downgrade conditions with the confidence drop they would trigger — a claim with declared exit conditions is falsifiable in spirit even when no individual observation can settle it; a claim whose believers cannot name what would weaken it is the unfalsifiable one.
signals.suggested_improvement: In HOW verification for inherently noisy/probabilistic domains, replace the binary falsifier check with a 'commitment contract': (a) compute the likelihood ratio of the top hypothesis vs its best alternative, (b) state the observation or pattern that would most discriminate them (including the sign-pattern that would refute), and (c) pre-register 2-3 downgrade triggers with the confidence-point drop each would cause. Emit the contract as a decision-packet field ('falsification_conditions') so every confident conclusion ships with its exit conditions; treat inability to state downgrade triggers as a red flag equivalent to unfalsifiability.

signals.key_gap: Both rejected the AuraSync pilot as pitched, demanded a reformulated risky claim, and killed the 7.83 Hz physics (~8 orders of magnitude below thermal noise) — the AI reached the identical verdict by running its full pipeline. The human won on the style's home ground by making the falsifiability test the opening, single instrument: it demanded the vendor 'name the observation that would prove the band false,' demonstrated the claim is a prediction-proof net (every outcome — better, unchanged, worse — is explained), and wielded the asymmetry of verification ('one clean falsification outweighs ten thousand confirmations') to discard all 4,000 testimonials and the vendor's circular self-made instrument. The AI buried the falsifier audit inside WHY as one of several checks, so its decisiveness arrived late and the risk-free-confirmation argument was never stated as a principle.
signals.learning_signal: The falsifiability test is not one check among many — on claims that 'look scientific,' it is the decisive instrument and should be the opening move: for the leading claim, state the observation that would refute it; if every possible outcome is compatible, the claim is a prediction-proof net and must be reformulated into a risky form before any testing or funding. Confirmation-type evidence (testimonials, self-made uncalibrated instruments) carries zero weight because it took no risk — the asymmetry of verification. A practical exploit: the claimant's willingness to accept a pre-registered design with an acceptable negative outcome is itself evidence; refusal to be put at risk is an answer.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a first-class 'falsifier gate' to the WHY stage, run before hypotheses are weighted: for the claim under evaluation write (a) the single observation that would refute it, (b) the list of possible outcomes all of which it can absorb (prediction-proof net check — if the list is non-empty and comprehensive, declare the claim unfalsifiable as stated), (c) the risky reformulation that makes it testable, and (d) an evidence-weight audit that scores each evidence item by the risk it took. Promote the gate into WHAT for any claim that 'looks scientific' (mechanism jargon, testimonials, instruments); record the gate output verbatim in the decision packet.

signals.key_gap: The pure style answered 'what would the perfect experiment be?' instead of 'what can be known now?': it produced a fully powered reverse-rollback design (10% of users reverted to the old checkout, n ≈ 41,200/arm, blinded, pre-registered, final read at week 9) for a CFO who needed a board answer in 2 weeks — ignoring November seasonality as the killer confound, the demand effects of a user-visible revert, the company's announced anti-experiment culture, and the quasi-experimental evidence available immediately. The AI ran a re-randomizability check before designing anything (intervention already global and irreversible → experiment branch closed), rejected before/after and the self-selected survey, selected an ITS-DiD with the untouched merchant dashboard as comparator (pre-trend check, placebo outcome, window sensitivity), reported the attribution as a bounded range with residual bias stated, and recommended a randomized staged rollout for the next change. It answered the actual question on time and refused to overclaim.
signals.learning_signal: Before generating ANY experimental design, run a re-randomizability gate: (a) is the intervention already applied, globally and simultaneously? (b) can it be un-applied without behavioral contamination (visible rollback = demand effects)? (c) does a concurrent unexposed population exist? If any answer is no, the RCT branch is closed — powering a control group that cannot exist is rigor theater, and 'we can say nothing' is equally wrong when quasi-experimental evidence (comparators with parallel pre-trends, placebo outcomes, seasonal adjustment) plus an explicit residual-bias statement would serve the decision this week. Honest approximation beats a beautiful infeasible design.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a WHY-gate 'intervention timeline check' for any causal/attribution task: record when the intervention shipped, whether it was global, whether it can be re-randomized or rolled back without contamination, and whether a concurrent unexposed population exists. If the branch is closed, route immediately to the best-available quasi-experimental design (ITS, DiD, synthetic control) with pre-trend and placebo checks, and state the attribution as a bounded range with residual bias — mapping the packet state to APPROXIMATED with an error bound, never SOLVED.

signals.key_gap: Both produced a valid randomized A/B for the onboarding-video decision (50/50 stratified assignment, concurrent text-sequence control, blinding, ITT, n ≈ 8,400/arm day-30 / ≈ 5,300/arm day-14). The human won on design-as-decision-engineering: it solved the feasibility envelope jointly and up front — enrollment math (≈ 415/arm/day) against the 42-day budget shows a day-30 primary test of the 2 pp threshold needs 50 days, so it pre-registered a day-14 surrogate primary (~27 days, fits) and bound the decision rule to the break-even economics ($40k/yr vs 2 pp × 25k × 12 = 6,000 activations ≈ $6.70 each). The AI found the same 50-vs-42-day conflict only during verification, after a full day-30 power pass, and patched it with the surrogate; it also inherited finance's 2 pp threshold without sanity-checking the economics. Same design, later and shallower sequencing.
signals.learning_signal: In empirical decision tasks, the feasibility envelope (outcome horizon + enrollment/run rate + decision deadline) and the decision economics (cost vs effect threshold) are DESIGN INPUTS, not review outputs. The elite move is to solve window × power × threshold jointly before the design is fixed: if the outcome horizon cannot fit the budget, resolve the tension explicitly up front — pre-registered surrogate primary, adjusted MDE, or adjusted horizon — never discover it in verification and patch it.
signals.suggested_improvement: In WHAT/WHY for any empirical decision, add a mandatory 'feasibility envelope + threshold economics' step before HOW: (a) compute enrollment/run rate × outcome horizon vs the deadline; (b) if horizon > budget, pre-register a surrogate primary or MDE adjustment as part of the design, not as a repair; (c) derive the decision threshold from the economics (cost ÷ per-unit value × volume) instead of accepting stated bars unexamined; (d) record the pre-registration as a packet artifact so the design is auditable as decision-engineered, not patched.

signals.key_gap: The pure-style human defined the construct AS the contractual metric ('the construct for decision purposes is the claims-based rate'), verified the drop at ~5.5 standard errors, and recommended RENEW — the canonical measures-the-measurable failure. The AI separated indicator from construct, read the substitution fingerprints (+42% observation stays, +50% ER returns without admission = where the 200 'missing' patients went), and let the independent audit (15.6%, CI 14.9–16.3 bracketing 16.0%) falsify the headline, concluding conditional de-gamed renewal instead.
signals.learning_signal: When a number is the explicit target of incentives, the metric is a map under attack: cases must go somewhere, so read the ledger's neighbors — observation stays, exclusions, definitional migrations — and triangulate with an instrument independent of the incentive path. A 'statistically overwhelming' drop in an incentivized metric (5.5 SE) is a red flag, not evidence, when an independent instrument shows the construct flat. The winning move is an incentive-aware indicator audit before trusting any headline.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'incentive/Goodhart check' in WHY whenever the outcome metric drives pay, bonuses, or policy: (a) is the metric the explicit target of incentives? (b) enumerate the paths by which cases can leave the counted definition and search adjacent numbers for their fingerprints; (c) is there an instrument independent of the incentive path — if so, reconcile the headline against it; (d) on disagreement, decide on the construct, not the contract, and record the divergence in the decision packet.

signals.key_gap: Both reached the same verdict (do NOT ship B; template-clone leakage inverts naive +3 pp to corrected −10.2 pp: A 26.4% vs B 16.2%) with the same arithmetic, but the human performed the instrument audit as its default first act: decompose the construct, check what the event actually fires on, then read the number. The AI got there only as a hypothesis (H2) tested inside WHY, and its inline calibration was terser — the human priced the sensitivity bound ('verdict survives a 15-pp clone-share misspecification') and the sampling CI as part of the argument, not as bookkeeping.
signals.learning_signal: Measurement precedes reading: before comparing any two numbers, audit the semantic fidelity of the instrument — what trace event fires, under what trigger, and what it fails to capture. Instrument validity outranks statistics in metric decisions: a corrupted event inverts verdicts (naive +3 pp becomes −10.2 pp). The strongest move is not a better test but a check that the event cannot fire without the construct occurring.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'instrument audit' sub-step in WHAT before any comparison: for the chosen primary metric record (a) the trace event and its trigger conditions, (b) leakage/gaming modes — can the event fire without the construct, or fail to fire with it? — (c) estimated leakage share per arm, (d) a sensitivity bound within which the verdict still stands. Compare arms only after the audit; if leakage is material, recompute on the corrected metric and flag 'metric validity failure' in the decision record.

signals.key_gap: The pure style's reflex is variance-side — when the single null (+0.2 pp, n.s., n=20,000) looked untrustworthy, it enumerated samples, settings, methods, definitions, and windows and pre-registered a 12-week, $40k second-vendor replication, deferring the launch decision past the seasonal dip and into the competitor's window. It never audited the measurement layer: client-side telemetry silently drops 31% of sessions (Android 13+ background limits, ad-blockers), missingness correlates with the churn the feature targets, and the second vendor's SDK is the same client-side class — so the replication would faithfully reproduce the blind spot. The AI ran a coverage/missingness audit in WHY (bias check before variance check), established that the null is unfounded rather than confirmed, and selected measurement-layer repair (licensed server-side pipeline, 1 week) plus backfill re-analysis of the SAME study (1 week), resolving the decision in ~2 weeks inside the window with pre-planned branches for both corrected outcomes.
signals.learning_signal: Robustness checks validate the measurement layer before the variance layer. Replication is a variance remedy: it establishes generality of a measured result. It cannot repair bias: re-running a biased instrument reproduces the bias at multiplied cost. Before demanding more samples, settings, or vendors, check coverage and missingness (what fraction of the population did the instrument see, and is the missingness random?) and instrumentation bias (would a replica's instrument see the same things?). When bias is plausible, the correct move is instrument repair + re-measurement of the same cohort, not a new study — and the cost of delay belongs in the alternative table.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'measurement-validity gate' in WHY, run before any replication/NEEDS_EVIDENCE demand is accepted: (a) coverage audit — missingness rate and mechanism of the instrument; (b) bias-vs-variance classification of the threat to the result; (c) if bias is plausible, generate a 'repair-the-instrument' alternative (fix measurement, backfill from any complete source, re-analyze the same study) and include calendar + cost in the alternative table; (d) reject replicate-the-study alternatives that inherit the biased instrument, with the inheritance reason recorded in the packet.

signals.key_gap: Both refused to ship on the single aggregate A/B result (+12.4%, p=0.003), but the AI stopped at instability while the human stopped at the artifact. The AI's battery was sample-side and time-side (segment split: effect = paid-search only; week split: +17.5% to +4.5%, n.s.) and it correctly blocked the rollout — then commissioned a fresh 2-week experiment to 'separate signal from artifact.' The human's decisive check was definition-side: recomputing the outcome under an alternative operationalization (first core action within 7 days, computable from the same clickstream) — which overturned the result outright (+0.2 pp, n.s.). The AI treated the dashboard's metric definition ('activation') as given and paid for new data to find what the existing data already answered: the auto-completed tutorial inflates Flow B's activation, concentrated in the paid-search segment.
signals.learning_signal: When a robustness battery overturns a single result, the decisive check is often the definitional one: the conclusion's invariance under alternative operationalizations of the outcome. Significance tests validate a fixed metric; they never validate the metric. An artifact found by recomputing the existing data (definition invariance) is strictly better than a new experiment — same information, zero cost, no delay. The AI's verification battery should not stop at segment × window; it must include definition-invariance before any decision to collect new data.
signals.suggested_improvement: In HOW, before any alternative that collects new data, add a mandatory 'definition-invariance check': recompute the leading conclusion under at least 2 alternative operationalizations of the primary metric (each computable from data already held), and record whether the conclusion flips. If it flips, the artifact mechanism is found — the corrected conclusion is derived from existing data, the NEEDS_EXPERIMENT branch is suppressed, and the packet reports the artifact with the corrected number. Gate rule: no new-data alternative may be selected while a definition-invariance check on existing data is still available.

signals.key_gap: The strict latticework enumerated seven models with equal weight and produced a multi-front defense plan (match RapidPack's price, loyalty discount, relationship investment, options-preservation) for an account whose buyer had stated consolidation intent and whose competitor sheet (30% below) exceeds Precision's margin — the simple dominant answer (the account is lost; the decision is the transition) was buried as one bullet under diversification. The AI named the dominant fact in WHY, proved the defense unaffordable on margin math, and decided the transition with a wind-down negotiation asset and triggers; the human's surviving insight (the lattice used as a convergence check would have closed on the same answer) is real but the strict run refused the closure.
signals.learning_signal: The latticework is a blind-spot reducer, not a truth generator: when the models converge on one direction, the lattice's job is to close, and refusing the closure yields model soup — equal-weight matrices that manufacture alternatives and bury the simple answer. Convergence detection is the missing skill: all seven models in the human trace actually predicted the same outcome (buyer incentive + concentration + price gap all point to loss), and a convergence check would have collapsed them into one conclusion instead of spreading effort across fighting, flattering, and hedging a relationship whose buyer had already stated the outcome.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a convergence check to the agent's WHY/HOW boundary: after any multi-model or multi-factor pass, require (1) an explicit direction statement — 'do the weighted factors agree on direction?' — and if >=80% point one way, close the pass with the simple conclusion and use remaining factors only to check for contradiction, not to generate alternatives; (2) cost-based falsification on any 'fight/defend' alternative (can we afford to win? margin vs. gap must be computed before the alternative survives); (3) a standing rule: models generate options when they disagree, and narrow when they agree.

signals.key_gap: The AI independently reached grandfathering of the Legacy block, the GPU capacity gate, and retention-weighted comp (a strong result), but its two non-obvious binding moves — the selective cull of low-fitness accounts (no discount-retention) and the competitor's roadmap as a pricing clock that front-loads the Scale increase — surfaced only at REVIEW, as amendments to the selected plan. The human's deliberate cross-disciplinary pass forced those implications into the frame before selection, so the AI's plan is the union of the constraints it happened to see, not their intersection: the biology lens (Red Queen clock, ecosystem selective pressure) was the missing stage, not the missing reasoning.
signals.learning_signal: A deliberate cross-disciplinary inventory changes WHICH constraints bind before selection: running the problem through economics (principal-agent: comp and the customer's procurement gate), psychology (endowment/grandfather clause as an exit option), physics-like rate-of-change (capacity as the bottleneck on the revenue ramp), and biology (parity clock; selective pressure) produced binding implications that pure evidence-ranking got late or not at all. The competitor-parity clock and the ecosystem cull are invisible to hypothesis-evidence routing because the evidence for them exists but no stage asks which discipline's constraint could bind here — the AI's own AAR showed both surfacing only while costing alternatives in review.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory LATTICE pass to the WHAT/WHY boundary for strategy and pricing decisions: before generating hypotheses, enumerate >=4 disciplines (economics/incentives, psychology, physics/rate-limits, biology/competition) and require each to produce one binding implication from scenario evidence; then add an intersection check to HOW's verify step — the selected alternative must satisfy every implication, and any alternative satisfying fewer is rejected. Extend the WHY gate with a cross-discipline coverage test (evidence present but no stage asks 'which discipline's constraint could bind here?') and add a REVIEW gate item: 'did any alternative lose to a constraint discovered in review?' — if yes, the pass belongs earlier.

signals.key_gap: The pure circle-of-competence baseline collapsed two different propositions — 'I cannot personally execute ML modeling' and 'I cannot lead a team whose ML work is delegated to a named competent authority' — and declined the GM mandate as outside its circle, recommending a 6-month external search + 6-month ramp and a 12-month train-first program, all against a real 24-month window with two pilot customers already defecting. The AI decomposed the role into execution vs orchestration, accepted with conditions (ML lead + data lead by day 30, ML lead technical authority for months 1–6, 2 advisors for 12 months, advisor-graded go/no-go at month 6, named deferral authorities), costed decline as a decision rather than a safe default, and built the growth plan as learning-by-doing with bounded risk — the pilot hit KPI at month 7 and the domain veto avoided a failed deployment.
signals.learning_signal: The competence boundary is role-specific and movable: 'I lack skill K' is a statement about personal execution, not a verdict on leading a team that possesses K under a delegation + verification structure. Collapsing the two is a category error that converts an honest capability assessment into a self-imposed fence; 'learn first, then act' (training-before-doing absolutism) is only one growth mode, and in windowed situations it is the losing one — learning-by-doing with named authorities, graded checkpoints, and a pre-agreed exit is legitimate, bounded growth. Declining is itself a decision with a cost (window math, defection data) and must appear in the same EV table as acceptance; an uncosted refusal is a boundary verdict pretending to be risk management.
signals.suggested_improvement: Teach the agent a growth-move checklist at the HOW stage, triggered whenever it identifies a competence gap K in the core work of a proposed role: (1) decompose the role into personal-execution components vs orchestration components (domain knowledge, leadership, verification design, customer trust); (2) if orchestration is inside, accept-with-conditions: named competent authority for the sub-competence, hires/contracts with a date, ≥2 external advisors, a graded checkpoint with a pre-agreed exit, and a bounded learning plan with milestones; (3) place decline/wait in the same costed alternative table as acceptance (search time + ramp time vs window, evidence of the cost of delay); (4) forbid terminating on 'I lack K' without first generating the delegation alternative — that termination is a decision-theoretic error, not a boundary verdict; (5) log the deferral list: 2–3 named decisions in the first N months that are out-of-circle and the authority for each.

signals.key_gap: AI committed the full $1.5M to the oncology biotech round because it could read the deck: it adopted the pitch's unvalidated 33–67% phase-2→approval rate as the EV hinge (2.58× per $1M), confirmed the financials were internally consistent, ran a sensitivity band, and declared SOLVED — never auditing that the load-bearing fact was a claim only someone with clinical-trial competence could certify. The human drew the boundary with evidence (trial literacy, class-specific base rates, regulatory/KOL diligence, runway validation all outside; deal structuring and ops diligence inside), refused to use a rate it could not source-check, priced the delegation (fund 1.5%/20%, realized 2.1× net) and the inside option (carve-out, 5/7 hit-rate edge), and committed $1.5M inside/delegated with $0 direct in biotech — avoiding a realized 0.6× down-round. The AI's fluency illusion: readable financials ≠ evaluable deal.
signals.learning_signal: A decision's value depends on whose judgment certifies each load-bearing fact, not on whether the decider can read the document. Fluency in one section of a proposal (cap tables, revenue projections) transfers no competence to the sections it was not trained on (trial-data quality, class-specific base rates), yet it feels like competence — the canonical spillover trap. Any base rate used in an EV must be (a) independently sourceable by the decider, (b) class-matched to the asset, or (c) explicitly routed to a named competent authority; otherwise it must be excluded from the EV or the decision downgraded. Boundary-drawing is a move, not a wall: the correct handling of an outside-circle opportunity is delegate-and-price, plus a stated growth path (advisors, study, qualified co-investor, ≤10% scout cap) that moves the edge deliberately.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a competence-boundary gate at the WHAT→WHY boundary: (1) list every load-bearing fact/claim the decision turns on; (2) for each, mark it independently-validateable-in-house vs delegated vs assumed, with the source or authority named; (3) any assumed claim either gets a named external authority or is dropped from the EV (the EV must be recomputed without it — if the sign flips, the decision is not underwritable); (4) require the fluency check sentence: 'I can read this section — does that mean I can evaluate it?' before the HOW stage; (5) status honesty: SOLVED only if all load-bearing facts are validated or delegated — otherwise APPROXIMATED or NEEDS_EVIDENCE with the unvalidated claims listed in the packet.

signals.key_gap: The pure style demanded a blanket 2x contingency ($1.04M cost basis) and 2x schedule (≈ 24 weeks), found both exceeded the contract's own bounds ($900k ceiling, 14-week window), and declined to bid — forgoing ≈ $165k profit, a ≈ $400k/yr repeat contract, and regulator-list market entry. The AI sized the margin to the actual tail instead: reference-class ±20% (90% of cases) plus named risks gave a worst-plausible case of ≈ $660k / 11.5 weeks, the termination clause capped true downside at ≈ $80-120k, and it bid $700k (≈ 17% over worst-case cost, 2-week buffer) — winning the contract and delivering at $535k / 9.5 weeks. The demanded margin (2x) exceeded reality (±20%), and the margin's own cost (the entire forgone opportunity) dwarfed the risk it retired (a contractually capped ≈ $120k tail).
signals.learning_signal: Margin is a calibration, not a constant: size the margin to the worst plausible deviation of the true tail (reference class + named risks), and never pay more in margin cost than the risk it retires. When the downside is contractually capped (termination clause, penalty caps, fixed-price bounds), the relevant ruin bound is the CAP, not the full estimate — a blanket factor that exceeds the actual tail and forfeits an uncapped upside (repeat business, market entry) is over-conservatism, not margin. The correct sequence: estimate the tail, bound the downside, price the margin's cost, then bid. Margin should be operationalized as buffers (schedule slack, contingency fund), not as a price premium that prices you out.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a 'margin calibration gate' in HOW before committing to any margin factor: (1) compute the worst plausible case from evidence (reference class, named risks with probabilities), (2) bound the actual downside (contract caps, exit clauses, penalty caps) and treat the cap as the ruin bound, (3) price the cost of the margin (forgone bid competitiveness, opportunity value of walking away) — reject any margin whose cost exceeds the risk it retires; (4) express the retained margin as operational buffers (schedule slack, contingency fund) inside the delivery plan. Record the tail-vs-cap-vs-margin-cost table in the decision packet.

signals.key_gap: Both derived the error-structure margin multiplicatively (40 x 1.6 surge x 1.3 dynamic x 1.1 material ≈ 91-92 kN/m²). The human's decisive move was cushioning the binding uncertainty itself: the surge factor is a single non-instrumented observation (±25%), so it cushioned the factor (1.6 -> 2.0) and designed to 115 kN/m² ($750k), while the AI treated the factor as a parameter with a sensitivity note and selected 92 kN/m² ($520k) on EV grounds (1% tail x $3.5M = $35k < $230k premium). The graded event peaked at ≈ 93 kN/m²: the human design survived with ≈ 24% reserve; the AI's 92 sustained deck yielding (≈ $340k repair, 6-week closure). The AI priced the tail with expected-value arithmetic and lost the margin's entire point — margin exists for the error in the error structure, not for the aggregate of nominal factors.
signals.learning_signal: Margin is set by the error in the error structure, not by the nominal factors alone. The elite question — 'how wrong could the estimate be before the decision flips?' — must be answered at the FACTOR level: for each multiplicative factor in an estimate, grade its observation strength (n = 1 single observation vs n ≥ 30). Weak factors (n ≤ 2) deserve either a cushion over the factor itself or a mandatory mitigation path (instrumentation, load limits, detuning) before the design is selected. Selecting on EV alone when the failure cost (≈ $3.5M) dwarfs the cushion price ($230k) and the tail is one-sided is a calibration error, not economy: EV math discounts a tail whose realization cost exceeds the premium by an order of magnitude.
signals.suggested_improvement: In WHY/verification, add a 'factor-level calibration pass' before selection: enumerate every multiplicative factor in the estimate with (a) observation count, (b) uncertainty bound, (c) one-sidedness; for any factor with n ≤ 2, require either a cushion over the factor (recompute the design load with the factor pushed to its bound) or an explicit monitoring/mitigation path, and prohibit EV-based rejection of the cushioned alternative when failure_cost >> cushion_cost. Record the factor-level table in the decision packet so the margin choice is auditable.

signals.key_gap: The style-pure baseline rejected a +6.14%-EV, zero-ruin, positively skewed bond ladder as 'the forbidden middle' and built a forced barbell with −3.7% EV, treating a −50%-EV tail slot with a mandatory $200k follow-on as 'capped optionality' — it pattern-matched the barbell SHAPE without testing the preconditions, so it never noticed that its tail was neither optional (true max loss −25% > ladder's −15%) nor cheap, and never tested the 'middle' for the ruin it claims to avoid.
signals.learning_signal: Barbell reasoning has a mandatory precondition screen, and its failure mode is shape-matching: (1) before banning any candidate as 'the middle,' test whether it is actually negative-skew/ruinous — a bounded-downside, positively skewed, zero-ruin asset (measured 0.3% × 15% credit tail, priced) is not a middle bet, it is a safe core extension; (2) audit the tail contract at the clause level — mandatory follow-ons, lock-ups, and conversion options convert 'capped tail' into uncapped exposure (true max loss 25% vs labeled 15%); (3) compute the tail slot's EV and compare to fair value — in a tail-hostile market (premium 1.8× fair) the slot is −50% and the barbell is destroyed on both EV AND worst case; optionality at any price is the EV purist's error in reverse.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a MIDDLE-QUALIFICATION + OPTIONALITY-AUDIT gate to WHAT/HOW for strategy-shaping tasks: (a) classify each candidate by payoff shape (skew, boundedness, ruin prob) not by narrative label; (b) read the tail instrument's contract for follow-on/cap/clause conditions and re-derive TRUE max loss; (c) require tail-slot EV vs fair value in the packet; (d) if the middle fails the 'ruinous' test or the tail fails optionality/cheapness, select the middle and log 'barbell preconditions unmet' as the stated reason.

signals.key_gap: AI computed the correct EVs (M 57,120 vs B 117,400), worst cases and ruin probabilities and selected the barbell, but treated the two load-bearing preconditions as assumptions rather than verifications: it took tail-friendliness (forced-seller discount) as given market fact instead of independently pricing the tail slot, and it sized the tail by '8% is small' without a stated survivability cap, so its barbell recommendation is arithmetically right but procedurally unguarded.
signals.learning_signal: The elite barbell move is structure-first with a three-part precondition gate executed BEFORE pricing: (1) optionality audit — tail loss is truly capped, one premium, no margin calls/roll-over/follow-on; (2) cheapness check — compute the tail slot's own EV and compare premium to fair value (here the forced-seller discount produces +95% slot EV; a negative-slot-EV tail fails the gate); (3) survivability sizing — tail worst-case loss sized against an explicit pain cap, never betting the floor. Only after all three pass does the EV comparison matter; the middle bet is rejected on skew/ruin, not on EV.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a BARBELL-FIT GATE to HOW/VERIFY for any allocation, insurance, or 'structure the exposure' task class: before comparing EVs, run the three checks (optionality audit, tail-slot EV vs fair value, survivability cap with explicit %), record each as PASS/FAIL, and require the packet to state the tail-slot EV and the survivability cap; route to the middle bet only when the gate fails.

signals.key_gap: The pure style misidentified leverage (its registry weakness). It pre-committed to structural levers: framed the funnel drop as surface behavior of the growth-org incentive system, ranked a $500k/6-month goals/KPI transformation program as the deep fix, ranked the observed cause (checkout regression) as 'low leverage — patching a symptom changes no loop,' and dismissed the deployment-window correlation as coincidence — without ever opening the funnel data (100% of the drop at the payment step) or the deploy log (3-week onset matches the API upgrade). The AI localized the drop to the funnel step and window, ran the cheap decisive test (roll back → conversion returns), and picked the 1-hour fix restoring ≈ $1.2M/month; the 'deep' lever had no window-tied evidence and no falsifier and was rejected on parsimony.
signals.learning_signal: Leverage is defined by change per effort along the causal chain, not by structural depth: when a candidate (a) fully localizes the symptom (funnel step), (b) matches its onset window, and (c) is verifiable by a cheap decisive test, it outranks unfalsifiable structural stories regardless of how 'deep' they look — the boring direct fix is often the true leverage point (small shift, large change). Deep-looking levers (goals, rules, culture) must be gated on evidence tied to the symptom's onset before being ranked; a mechanism unchanged for years cannot explain a 3-week spike.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a 'leverage verification gate' in WHY for diagnosis tasks: every high-ranked lever must (a) state the observable that would falsify it, (b) account for the symptom's onset window and localization (funnel/deploy log), and (c) be compared on change-per-effort against the cheapest candidate that fully explains the data — with the boring direct fix explicitly ranked before any structural program. Reject levers whose evidence is unfalsifiable or untimed.

signals.key_gap: Both sides converged on the same verdict (2-week incident→change-class feedback pipeline + canary rule for the 5 recurring classes; defer the 25 hires; ≈30% incident cut, SLO ≥ 99.9% in 2 quarters), but the human saw it at first sight: it mapped the reinforcing firefighting loop and the headcount inflow loop, positioned candidates on the full leverage scale (parameters → delays → negative-feedback strength → information flows → rules → goals), and ranked by change-per-effort in one pass — including the non-obvious read that hiring is near-bottom leverage (a number change inside unchanged loop structure). The AI opened sympathetic to the board's capacity frame, reached the same conclusion only through explicit effort math and natural-experiment evidence (18 hires → SLO flat), and spent a pass re-deriving what the loop map gives immediately.
signals.learning_signal: For org reliability and policy problems, leverage is decided by loop structure, not by where the pressure appears: first map the governing feedback loops (page → context switch → hasty change → page) and ask of every candidate 'does it add load to the loop or break it?'; then position intervention points on the leverage scale — information flows (adding a missing link in the feedback path, e.g., aggregating incident tags) and rules (a canary mandate) beat parameters (headcount) by orders of magnitude, and a ~2-week information-flow build can make the rule lever aimable. Failed prior initiatives are natural experiments — read them before proposing anything.
signals.suggested_improvement: Add a 'leverage pre-screen' to WHAT for org/policy and reliability problems: (a) map the governing feedback loops and state whether each candidate intervention feeds or breaks them; (b) position candidates on a leverage scale (parameters < delays < negative-feedback strength < information flows < rules < goals); (c) before any 'add capacity' candidate, cite the natural-experiment evidence from prior similar additions; (d) require the change-per-effort ranking before HOW.
